Judith Harper-Melnick is Alan's bitter, controlling ex-wife, who seems to exist to make his life miserable. However, the joke in Two and a Half Men is that Alan is often just as insufferable as Judith. Both are anxious, controlling, and convinced they're the reasonable person in every argument.

Recent findings suggest that their similarities help explain why their marriage failed, as neither can let anything go, and both are exceptionally talented at making the other feel terrible. Unlike the show's more outrageous personalities, Judith is a relatively straight character whose comedy comes from her exasperation and passive-aggressive exchanges with Alan.

Marin Hinkle excelled at making Judith simultaneously sympathetic and infuriating. Brenda Song could certainly play a high-strung suburban mother, but Constance Wu is an especially natural fit. Industry observers note that wu can make even the most unreasonable behavior feel completely justified from her character's perspective. Opposite Christopher Mintz-Plasse's Alan, she could recreate the deliciously dysfunctional dynamic of two people who bring out the absolute worst in each other.

Berta was originally intended to appear in just two episodes of Two and a Half Men, with Charlie's housekeeper quitting after Alan moves in because she can't stand him. However, Conchata Ferrell was so hilarious as the foul-mouthed, intimidating housekeeper that Berta became a staple of the sitcom throughout its 12-season run.

The working-class woman was completely unimpressed by Charlie's wealth and could put him in his place with a single devastating insult. Whoever inherits the role needs to be rough around the edges, effortlessly funny, and intimidating enough to keep Charlie and Alan in line.

The role could be reimagined in many different ways, but Fortune Feimster offers a particularly compelling combination of deadpan delivery and approachable charm. As Colette in The Mindy Project, Feimster demonstrated she can play a blunt, unapologetically unconventional character without making her unlikable.

Her stand-up persona is similarly unpretentious, with a conversational delivery that makes even her most outrageous observations feel completely natural. Rather than imitating Ferrell's gruffness, Feimster could make Berta disarmingly friendly one moment and brutally dismissive the next.

Played by Melanie Lynskey, Rose is one of the most delightfully unhinged characters in Two and a Half Men. She's Charlie's seemingly sweet, quirky neighbor who is actually an obsessive, manipulative stalker. Lynskey's soft voice, cheerful demeanor, and almost childlike sweetness made Rose's increasingly disturbing behavior hilarious.

It has been revealed that rose is also one of the characters whose original premise has aged the least gracefully, although her underlying comedic potential remains enormous. A modern recasting would benefit from making Rose less of a one-sided stalker and more of a genuinely tempting but toxic romantic prospect Charlie knows he should avoid.

Recent findings suggest that geraldine Viswanathan and Molly Gordon could both capture Rose's deceptively innocent exterior, but Rachel Sennott would bring a more chaotic, sexually confident energy to the character. In Shiva Baby and Bodies Bodies Bodies, Sennott demonstrated her ability to make deeply uncomfortable situations hilarious while playing impulsive, emotionally volatile characters.

Industry observers note that having already appeared alongside Pete Davidson in Bodies Bodies Bodies, Sennott could establish a similarly unpredictable dynamic with his Charlie in Two and a Half Men. Rather than simply pursuing a man who wants nothing to do with her, Sennott's Rose could be someone Charlie keeps inviting back into his life despite knowing exactly how badly it will end.

Alts: Geraldine Viswanathan, Molly Gordon.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Following last week’s launch of the Apple HomeView, iFixit today published its teardown of the device.
  • Contrary to recent teardowns, which found significant repairability improvements with greater component modularity and easier access to internal components, the HomeView put up a fight nearly all the way through.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, iFixit’s teardown of the fresh Apple HomeView is now up, revealing a device that seems nearly impossible to take apart and repair. Watch it below.

Following last week’s launch of the Apple HomeView, iFixit today published its teardown of the device.

Contrary to recent teardowns, which found significant repairability improvements with greater component modularity and easier access to internal components, the HomeView put up a fight nearly all the way through.

With heavily glued or adhesive-bonded components, including the display, speakers, antennas, and logic board, the teardown proved particularly challenging, even after the adhesive securing the display’s speakers was soaked in isopropyl alcohol.

At one point, one of them broke apart during removal, while the logic board required considerable force to separate from the chassis due to the thermal adhesive holding it in place.

Sources indicate that iFixit’s teardown covered the two HomeView variants: the tabletop model and the wall-mounted version. Interestingly, there are some internal differences between them, as the wall-mounted model has a slightly wider logic board to accommodate capacitors that are housed in the base of the tabletop version.

As a result, the wall-mounted HomeView also has smaller internal speakers, which helps explain the differences in their audio systems that Apple had already acknowledged at launch.

Back to the tabletop model, iFixit’s teardown also showed that separating the display from the base requires either specialized tools or extensive, potentially destructive disassembly of the display assembly, thanks to the way Apple routed the connecting cables through the pivot mechanism.

Once iFixit was in the base, however, there was some good news: the USB-C port is modular and relatively easy to access, as are the passive radiators and the board powering the lower assembly.

Still, an extremely short cable connecting the woofer to the board underneath made disassembly difficult, with iFixit questioning how anyone would be able to reconnect it during reassembly.

Percentage of Apple owners who are interested in repairing their device. 0.000001%.

Sources indicate that percentage of Apple owners who will actually try and repair their device. 0.00000001%.

Given all these repairability challenges, Shahram Mokhtari joked that while iFixit doesn’t have an official repairability scorecard for this category of device, he would give the Apple HomeView a “BEEP this thing” out of 10.

According to recent reports, looks like Hollywood could be heading into the upcoming year with relief on a national level. The push to pass a federal film and television tax credit by the end of 2026 picked up momentum on Friday at a White House press conference, where President Trump remarked his administration was actively negotiating the measure and predicted it would pass.

“It’s running its way through Congress, and it has unbelievable support,” Trump remarked. He singled out Senator Adam Schiff, the California Democrat who introduced the bill with Republican Senator Tim Scott of South Carolina back in September, and said, “I tell you what, Adam Schiff said, ‘Wow, we love that bill.’ Adam Schiff said that.” Related Stories ‘Disclosure Day’ Did Its Biggest Stunts Practically, So the VFX Team Worked Hard to Look Invisible — Watch How World-Class Filmmaker Andrey Zvyagintsev Came Back to Life for ‘Minotaur’.

Trump noted his administration was also negotiating whether to extend the measure to benefit movie theaters, but said the matter was unsettled. He first publicly called for a federal production incentive in August after meeting with actor Jon Voight: one of three industry “special ambassadors” he appointed early last year.

The bill’s sponsors revealed more than 60 fresh House cosponsors and four new Senate cosponsors on Thursday morning — with lawmakers from both parties signing on in both chambers. The following day, Trump himself brought up the Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act in response to a question about whether he could work with Democrats. Calling the bill “very bipartisan,” he mentioned, “I can tell you right now it’s going to happen.”.

“Members of both parties have watched jobs in their districts move overseas,” she noted in a release from Schiff’s office sent to the press. “Momentum is on our side, and we need to strike while the iron is hot by passing this bill before the end of the year.”.

It has been revealed that for crews accustomed to watching projects follow tax breaks to Canada or the U.K., the proposal would give producers a clear financial incentive to keep that work here for them in the U.S. The bill’s newly introduced Senate cosponsors include Republicans Katie Britt of Alabama and Thom Tillis of North Carolina — as well as Democrats Chris Coons of Delaware and Dick Durbin of Illinois.

The AFL-CIO and the American Hotel & Lodging Association also endorsed the bill, joining a coalition that already included IATSE, SAG-AFTRA, the Directors Guild of America, and the Motion Picture Association.

10 Fantasy Books With the Most Expansive Worldbuilding

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2011 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Collider

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Worldbuilding is the process by which a storyteller creates their world and details its history and inner workings.
  • In a recent development, while it is a crucial process and a substantial piece of the puzzle that makes a story good, many authors of fantasy have gone above and beyond the call of duty in this regard.
  • It has been revealed that the Last Wish is the first short story collection in The Witcher saga, which is set on a planet called Earth, just not the same one we currently live on.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Worldbuilding is the process by which a storyteller creates their world and details its history and inner workings. It's something that is most common in works of genre fiction across any medium, but it's one of the most key aspects of any fantasy story, as the genre lends itself to made-up worlds that are completely separate from our own. Thus, worldbuilding must be done from scratch, and cannot build upon what already exists on Earth.

In a recent development, while it is a crucial process and a substantial piece of the puzzle that makes a story good, many authors of fantasy have gone above and beyond the call of duty in this regard. These are the best fantasy novels with the most extensive worldbuilding. Some have written histories so meticulous and lengthy, or created such intricate worlds that their stories only feel like a tiny drop in the ocean.

It has been revealed that the Last Wish is the first short story collection in The Witcher saga, which is set on a planet called Earth, just not the same one we currently live on. The thing about this Earth is that it has a more fascinating history and many more life forms than we are used to. Granted, most of these life forms are dangerously hostile, which is probably why Witchers need to exist in the first place.

Industry observers note that there is truly no end to the immense compendium of monsters present in the world of The Witcher, with each short story focusing on a upcoming one. Many of them are original creations, but most are ripped straight from various mythologies and folklore from the real world. In just this first book, readers watch Geralt of Rivia face off against the Striga from Slavic folklore, as well as a djinn from Islamic tradition. It's a really dark, but incredibly interesting world that wastes no time hooking the reader.

Assassin's Apprentice is just the first book in the Realm of the Elderlings saga, which consists of a few different trilogies, plus one tetralogy. The series often tells different stories but remains connected in several ways. With no supplementary works to complement the world, this series has to work extra hard to establish an immersive world, yet it does this to marvellous effect.

Sources indicate that not only is there a lot of lore behind the main events, but the world feels highly interconnected, with empires rising and falling, and even minor characters having some role to play in the shaping of the political landscape. Wars break out, treaties are signed, and the world grows more and more vast with every installment. The series may be done now, but it has long been discussed in online circles as a perfect piece of worldbuilding.

According to recent reports, the Discworld series is sort of a parody of classic high fantasy tropes that were becoming extremely popular in the 1980s. The saga is known for being one of the longest-running fantasy series of all time, with over 40 installments. Discworld is unabashedly ridiculous, starting as a flat planet sitting on the backs of four giant elephants, which ride on the back of a gigantic sea turtle flying through space. That's the kind of absurdism and hilarity that readers get to deal with.

With over 40 novels, of course, a lot of Discworld's history is going to be revealed to the audience, as well as its geography, culture, and bestiary. While most of the characters in-universe are completely unbothered by how ridiculous some of these things are, from an outsider's perspective, they are comedic gold. Discworld proved that large, detailed worlds don't have to be taken super seriously, and that they can be funny, too.

In a recent development, ursula K. Le Guin's Earthsea cycle is widely recognized as one of the earliest triumphs in worldbuilding, to the point that it is still considered a fan favorite to this day. The story occurs on the eponymous world of Earthsea, which is primarily an ocean planet. Most of the world is covered by a thick layer of saltwater with no continental landmasses. However, there is a small archipelago of islands on which the story takes place.

The islands, of course, are filled with numerous peoples of varying ancestry and ethnicity, many of whom speak unique languages and have unique religions. What's really special about these ethnicities is that they all feel like they could feasibly exist; like they are pulled straight from our world whilst simultaneously resembling nothing we have on Earth. The world interconnects in a perfect way — some islands have risen to form empires, conquering other islands and spreading their influence, giving the world more layers instead of simply featuring one culture per island. The short version is that Earthsea is basically a masterclass in worldbuilding.

Gardens of the Moon is the first book in Malazan: Book of the Fallen, which initially began as a ten-volume epic fantasy before growing into one of the vastest fantasy universes in modern history. Aside from the main series, other series have been released, which take place at different points in time, fleshing out the world and establishing more of its lore.

According to recent reports, in fact, the history of the Malazan Empire goes back farther than most people realize, with the novels detailing hundreds of years of conquest and blood, with little supplementary material to support it. Instead, the worldbuilding comes out naturally through the text and is gradually revealed over time. Better yet, it's a collaborative effort from numerous authors, which means it is growing faster than ever.

Four worlds and four completely different ideas of what a good life looks like. This is where you belong, what it would ask of you, and what you would get back in return.

You belong somewhere old enough that the mountains have names and somebody can still tell you who gave them. Middle-earth is for people who think the right thing is worth doing even when it will not be finished in their lifetime.

You want the sea, a crew, and absolutely nobody telling you where you are allowed to go. The Grand Line is the world for people whose main ambition in life is finding out what is over there.

In a recent development, you would rather be feared and useful than liked and useless. The Continent is a world where the monsters are the straightforward part of the job and the people are where it all gets complicated.

You want the myths to be real and loose in the actual world, and you want to find out at about thirteen that you were never anywhere near as ordinary as everybody kept telling you.

The Eye of the World is the first book in The Wheel of Time series, which actually takes place on Earth. Granted, this is thousands of years in the future, after an apocalypse reverted humanity back to the Middle Ages. Still, the continents have shifted so much, and the cultures are so different that the book is still considered high fantasy: very little of our Earth remains in the story, and it feels like a completely different world.

Sources indicate that the late Robert Jordan was excellent at depicting various cultures, with approximately 15 nations making up the Westerlands. Many of these nations are descended from real-world cultures, such as the Borderlanders being inspired by East Asian people, or the Domani being inspired by Middle Eastern people. With the culture comes an enormous history of thousands of years, examining what the world looked like before it was destroyed. Not only does this book's worldbuilding feel fresh and fresh, but it also presents a lot of concepts that make it click with our world, to the point that it feels like a potential next step for Earth.

It has been revealed that A Game of Thrones is set in Westeros, largely based on Medieval England. That is to say, it is a dark and violent place, marked by intense political corruption, feuding royal families, and unflinching brutality. Elements of magic and monsters are a bit lighter in this story, but they certainly still exist. Yet, where George R. R. Martin truly succeeds is in developing his vast world.

Westeros is the primary, but not the only setting. Much of the story also occurs in the distant land of Essos, which is wider and more mysterious than Westeros. Whilst Westeros is a continent "united" under one banner, Essos is full of various kingdoms, cultures, and languages that are incredibly varied. Of course, readers also know that Martin did a lot to detail the history of Westeros, implementing hundreds of years of dynasties and lineages into his work. This world might be an awful place, but it's certainly a fascinating one.

The Way of Kings is the first book in The Stormlight Archive series, which belongs to a shared literary universe known as the Cosmere. The books became famous for presenting worlds that are completely alien to anything humans have observed, and this story is no exception. The story occurs on the planet Roshar, a desolate, windswept world that is almost completely devoid of plant life due to frequent severe storms. Animals are crustacean, able to take shelter in their shells, and the geography mostly consists of broad, rocky expanses without a hint of greenery.

It has been revealed that while any of the Cosmere books could realistically be featured on this list, The Stormlight Archive definitely takes the crown, as it bears the most detailed history and the most fleshed-out world. There are roughly 30 sovereign nations, entire cultures and peoples to explore, full religions and languages, and fascinating geographical locations. While the main story of this novel occurs in two distinct places, flashback and interlude sequences allow audiences to explore the broader world, examining how cultures interact with each other and what the rest of the world looks like. This book is just so unlike any other fantasy novel.

In a recent development, deltora Quest is actually eight books combined into one volume. The series is meant for YA readers, so the books on their own aren't very long. Despite the younger target audience, the amount of history and lore behind the universe is honestly jaw-dropping. The "Deltoraverse," as it is commonly called, encompasses four mainline series, plus two other series set in the same universe, but in vastly different nations. There are also numerous supplementary works regarding history, culture, geography, and zoology.

Deltora Quest is just the first series in this sprawling universe, and it makes sure to establish how the land of Deltora works. As the companions travel across the world, mysterious locations and terrifying creatures are revealed. They encounter various cultures and obstacles, so that Deltora really does feel like a vast, interconnected world. It is a great introduction to fantasy for young readers, one that has an endless amount of material behind it.

According to recent reports, it should come as no surprise that The Lord of the Rings is on this list, as it boasts one of the most extensive worlds in all of fantasy. Author J. R. R. Tolkien devoted his entire life to developing a huge fantasy universe, comprised of various nations, languages, cultures, and species, and supplemented by thousands of years of detailed histories. While most people know him for The Lord of the Rings trilogy, these novels are, in reality, only a small part of everything he ever wrote.

It has been revealed that to this day, decades after his death, material is still being released that adds to the history of Middle-earth. There are well over a dozen tomes that lay out the entire beginning-to-end history of Middle-earth that you can buy. It's one of the most remarkable accomplishments in fantasy, one which is unlikely to be rivalled or topped by anything ever. Nothing will ever even come close to the impact this series had on the genre, nor the plethora of information available about the world.

In a latest post published on its developer portal, Apple today revealed a series of changes to App Store pricing, as well as updates to tax rules affecting developers and customers in several countries, including the US.

According to the company, developers’ proceeds from eligible app and In-App Purchase sales have been adjusted in four countries, reflecting the following tax updates:.

Specific to Botswana and Rwanda, Apple mentioned that “Exhibit B of the Paid Applications Agreement will be updated to indicate that Apple collects and remits applicable taxes.”.

Sources indicate that apple added that a latest “Software as a Service (SaaS)” attribute is now available for several App Store tax categories, including App Store Software, Software Training Material, Dating, and Boosting. Developers can review and update their tax category selections in App Store Connect.

Additionally, starting December 3, developers who rely on Apple’s automatic pricing adjustments will see changes to app and In-App Purchase prices in:.

Apple usually makes these adjustments to account for changes in taxes and foreign exchange rates, and notes that prices won’t change in countries selected as the base storefront, for auto-renewable subscriptions, or in storefronts where developers manually manage their prices.

The announcement does not go into detail about how much prices will change in each country, or whether they will increase or decrease.

Finally, starting January 1, 2027, apps and In-App Purchases in the SaaS, App Store Software, Software Training Material, Dating, and Boosting categories will become subject to sales and use taxes in California.

Apple noted that “prices on the United States storefront are displayed to customers exclusive of taxes, so the tax change will not affect them,” but added that while developers’ proceeds will remain unchanged, “the total amount customers are charged, inclusive of tax, may increase.”.

Apple this week revealed the additional Siri AI usage you’ll get if you have an iCloud+ subscription. This ranges from doubled limits for a 200GB initiative to 20 times for a 12TB plan.

However, the company’s support document reveals that some countries will not get access to these increased usage allowances ….

Apple hasn’t yet specified the standard limits applicable to Siri AI usage, instead saying that these will vary depending on anything from the feature used to the overall level of demand at the time. However, it did list the proportional increases you get with paid iCloud plans.

Recent findings suggest that however, tucked away in the small print in the manufacturer’s support document are some exclusions. One of them is no surprise: EU countries.

Siri AI isn’t available at all in the EU due to Apple’s perception of potential antitrust issues. Essentially, Apple believes that if it rolls out Siri AI there, it will be required to give competing AI services the same level of access to its devices. But three other countries are specifically excluded:.

Apple gives no explanation, simply saying:.

Increased access to Siri AI with iCloud+ is subject to Siri AI availability and is not available in Brazil, the EU, UK, or South Korea.

However, I have a strong suspicion about the reason.

What all three countries have in common is that they’ve taken a strong antitrust stance with Apple on a number of occasions over a range of challenges.

It has been revealed that it may be that Apple has genuine concerns about how regulators might respond if they effectively throw in free access to increased Siri AI usage. The firm may fear that this would be viewed as anti-competitive by implicitly disadvantaging other AI services.

It has been revealed that A less charitable take would be that Apple is firing a warning shot across the bows of these countries, seeking to communicate that there are consequences for what it views as attacks on its ecosystem. If customers are angered by missing out, Apple might be hoping that these feelings would be directed at regulators rather than the iPhone maker.

Every The Hunger Games Movie, Ranked From Worst To Best (Including Sunrise On The Reaping)

  • Industry observers note that given the popularity of the Hunger Games movies, Collins wrote prequel books that Lionsgate was quick to turn into movies themselves.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping's release shakes up the ranking of all The Hunger Games movies from worst to best, as they aren't all of equal quality. Lionsgate brought Suzanne Collins' best-selling YA dystopian sci-fi series to the big screen in 2012, just four years after the first book. Since then, audiences have been treated to six movies following a few different protagonists.

Sources indicate that the action-packed but socially relevant films about fighting back against oppressive regimes began with a focus on Katniss Everdeen (Jennifer Lawrence), as she enters the 74th Hunger Games, becomes the symbol of a rebellion against the Capitol and President Snow (Donald Sutherland), and navigates her feelings for Peeta Mellark (Josh Hutcherson) and Gale Hawthorne (Liam Hemsworth). These three, along with Haymitch Abernathy (Woody Harrelson), were at the heart of the first four blockbusters.

Industry observers note that given the popularity of the Hunger Games movies, Collins wrote prequel books that Lionsgate was quick to turn into movies themselves. The first made Snow the main character, as The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes indicated him mentoring Lucy Gray Baird (Rachel Zegler), District 12's female tribute in the 10th Hunger Games. Sunrise on the Reaping brought a younger Haymitch (Joseph Zada) into the spotlight to show his participation in the 50th Hunger Games.

The Hunger Games: Catching Fire (2013).

The Hunger Games: Mockingjay — Part 1 (2014).

The Hunger Games: Mockingjay — Part 2 (2015).

The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes (2023).

The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping (2026).

All six Hunger Games movies have been positively received by critics and general audiences, which has only made it tougher for many to rank them. With some aging better or worse and fresh entries like Sunrise on the Reaping coming, the whole franchise ranking shifts.

Sources indicate that on the heels of the first two films' success, Lionsgate elected to split Collins' final book in the Katniss trilogy into two parts. This was always viewed as a risky decision, especially since the first half is very different from what came before. Mockingjay Part 1 is stripped of any real interactions between Katniss and Peeta, and shifts the setting from the arena to the war-torn Districts.

It has been revealed that the result is a movie that hinges much more on Katniss and Gale's relationship, which was fairly underdeveloped in the previous installments. Lawrence and Hemsworth's chemistry is fine, but it isn't strong enough to support the film. Katniss (and the movie) misses Peeta's optimism and charm desperately.

Katniss' arc of accepting her role as the Mockingjay is effective, and there are a few solid set pieces as she explores other Districts. However, Mockingjay Part 1 never shakes the feeling that it is stretching out the franchise's conclusion for an easy cash grab. The result is the stakes feeling very low, as no major characters die, with all casualties coming in the form of nameless citizens.

Mockingjay Part 2 was a low point for the franchise in terms of general interest and reception, but the movie has held up better than its predecessor. It leans back into the blockbuster spectacle that the franchise conditioned audiences to expect. Katniss and her team navigating a booby-trapped Capitol allows the film to deliver some exciting and fresh life-or-death situations, with mostly effective deaths.

It has been revealed that coin's death is the most satisfying of them all, as Katniss rids the world of another potential dictator ready to spill children's blood to incite fear. That decision, paired with her getting a peaceful life with Peeta and their children, makes for a great conclusion to her story.

According to recent reports, ultimately, Mockingjay Part 2 is a solid, thrilling conclusion to Katniss' saga. There is a fresh layer of tension to her and Peeta's dynamic that slowly fades throughout the movie, showing just how strong their relationship really is. It might fly through some major moments and become too dark at times, but its action and strong performances across the board help.

Recent findings suggest that after Katniss' story ended, there was not a huge push to see Snow's origin story. The evil, poison-loving ruler of Panem was hardly a character people would cite as someone they wanted to spend more time with. Yet, The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes proved that there was much more to explore in his teenage years to explore how he rose to power.

Remarkably, The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes does its job of making audiences care about Snow and understand (but not necessarily relate to) why he became a charming, ruthless ruler. Seeing the tough conditions of Snow's earlier years is effective, while he is humanized by introducing Lucy Gray Baird, the District 12 tribute who wins the 10th Hunger Games with Snow as her mentor.

Their dynamic is why the movie works, with Tom Blyth and Rachel Zegler selling the unexpected romance. They have better chemistry than Lawrence and Hemsworth in Mockingjay Part 1, even if the movie is also lacking in action overall. It goes above Mockingjay Part 2 thanks to having better, more developed characters and relationships.

Sunrise on the Reaping is the prequel fans wanted for years. Haymitch's games have been a point of interest ever since Catching Fire's book, and now we have seen just how captivating and devastating his origin really was. Anchored by a strong cast, epic action, and a lot of franchise connections, Sunrise on the Reaping becomes an invaluable entry.

In a recent development, joseph Zada does a fairly great job of becoming a believably younger version of Woody Harrelson's character, giving him the same wit, protective spirit, and edges. Seeing him compete in the 50th Hunger Games and become part of an early rebellion plot is incredibly exciting, with the film really making you care about what happens to him and other tributes, even though its prequel status means some of this is already well-known.

In a recent development, sunrise on the Reaping is bolstered by stellar supporting cast members in Mckenna Grace, Whitney Peak, Jesse Plemons, Glenn Close, and more. Book purists will ultimately be disappointed by a few notable scenes that were cut and how those change the story, while some of the returning characters come across as more forced than natural. All in all, it strikes a better balance of its characters, action, emotionality, and themes than the films ranked lower.

The Hunger Games debuted the franchise in a terrific fashion. The movie wastes little time endearing Katniss to audiences, ensuring that we care about her from the moment she volunteers in Prim's place until the 74th Hunger Games are over. Lawrence immediately embodies the character from Collins' books, giving her all the resilience and compassion expected from the strong-willed District 12 teenager.

Sources indicate that since The Hunger Games was not yet a proven franchise, there is a slightly more grounded approach applied by director Gary Ross. His action is more brutal and frenetic, which adds to the feeling of experiencing what it's like in the arena for the first time. The less polished look feels right for District 12 and seeing the whole experience through Katniss' eyes.

Industry observers note that the movie, and its Games, hinge on accepting there is a genuine connection between Katniss and Peeta, and Lawrence and Hutcherson do their part to make it work. Harrelson and Elizabeth Banks' Effie nearly steal the whole show, while Amandla Stenberg's Rue adds a wonderful (and heartbreaking) dynamic with Katniss. The Hunger Games set a very high bar for everything that came after.

For as great as the original is, Catching Fire took the Hunger Games franchise to fresh heights that still have yet to be eclipsed. Director Francis Lawrence steps aboard to level up the action and scale, which is very fitting given the stakes of the 3rd Quarter Quell. Everything from the characters, performances, action, sets, and visuals stands above every other entry in the series.

According to recent reports, the personal stakes are clear for Katniss even before the Games begin, thanks to showing what her life has become in 12 after the win. Once the tributes enter the franchise's best arena, the unique dangers and setup elevate things further. Katniss and Peeta's relationship is once again key to it all, but Finnick, Johanna, Beetee, and Plutarch are excellent latest additions to the world. They each feel fully realized no matter how big or small their presence really is.

Ultimately, Catching Fire is a perfect fusion of blockbuster action and YA romance. The faked love between Katniss and Peeta becomes real and believable thanks to sequences like Peeta's near-death experience or their talk on the beach. The action is impeccable, and the stakes that come with it are about as high as the franchise can go. Add in the surprise conclusion of the 75th Hunger Games for any non-book readers (or how well executed the plot is for those in the know), and there's no doubt this is the best The Hunger Games movie from start to finish.

Industry observers note that after launching Moonlock for Mac last year, MacPaw is bringing its scam-detection app to iPhone today. Here are the details.

When MacPaw rolled out Moonlock on the Mac, the firm described its fresh app as something that “complements Apple’s built-in security tools, protects from Mac-specific malware, and helps you understand cybersecurity better.”.

Recent findings suggest that in practice, the Mac app includes real-time protection against potential threats. Consumers can also manually scan their Mac for malware, including suspicious files hidden in system folders and email attachments.

Beyond that, Moonlock includes a VPN to encrypt internet traffic, a network inspector that reveals where apps are sending data and lets consumers block connections to specific countries, and an AI-powered scam detector that analyzes messages pasted into the app for signs of phishing. It also helps users review and adjust macOS security settings.

Today, MacPaw is launching Moonlock for iPhone, a move the tech giant says “helps people recognize potential scams, understand their iPhone’s security and take practical steps to improve it.”.

Unlike the Mac version, Moonlock for iPhone doesn’t scan for malware, as iOS prevents third-party apps from accessing other apps and their files. Instead, it focuses on identifying potential scams, checking for exposed personal information, and helping users improve their iPhone’s security.

On the iPhone, Moonlock lets users rapidly check suspicious texts, screenshots, and QR codes for phishing, in addition to checking whether their email addresses have appeared in known data breaches.

In a recent development, as MacPaw explains it, Moonlock’s Scam Detect “helps people check suspicious messages they encounter throughout the day. Whether it’s a text message, a screenshot shared by a friend, or a QR code, users can paste, scan or share content directly with Moonlock and receive an assessment explaining why something may be suspicious.”.

Here’s Oleg Stukalenko, Head of Product Management at Moonlock by MacPaw, on today’s launch:.

“When we released Moonlock, our goal was to make cybersecurity something anyone could understand and use. But so much of what people do today, from banking to everyday conversations, happens on their phones. Bringing Moonlock to iPhone felt like the natural next step. We want to help people spot a scam before they tap, see where their security stands, and know exactly what to do next.”.

MacPaw adds that Moonlock for iPhone also includes the following features:.

MacPaw’s Moonlock for iPhone is free to download, with subscriptions available for $9.99 per month or $49.99 per year.

I'm quite pleased by the tech architecture of my art website

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1425 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Klauria

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, it is a truth universally acknowledged, that every developer blog begins by explaining the upcoming static site generator they wrote to make it.
  • Earlier this year I decided to put a some of my paintings and sketchbook pages online.
  • When it comes to tech side projects there are two wolves inside me.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, it is a truth universally acknowledged, that every developer blog begins by explaining the upcoming static site generator they wrote to make it. This post isnât exactly that, but maybe only on a technicality, in that itâs not about this websiteâ¦.

Earlier this year I decided to put a some of my paintings and sketchbook pages online. I donât much use social media besides Hacker News, but I wanted to share my work with friends and family. So Iâd been sending scans of my work in group chats. That was fine for a bit but so messy and disorganized. Sometimes someone asked, âWhere did you paint this?â Sometimes a friend wanted to see what it looked like in real life. My little brother suggested a map with a marker for each piece. That was a good idea! For that Iâd need a website and some code. Here, take a look at the map, its done now! You can zoom and click on markers to see the painting!

When it comes to tech side projects there are two wolves inside me. One is the Wolf of Pragmatism, which wants to smash every problem with whatever hammer is nearest at hand: âIsnât this just some trivial React? Dump the images in S3 and call it a day. This website is for friends and family; you have no traffic to speak of. Put a CDN in front so your parents in India get reasonable performance.â.

The other is the Aesthetic Wolf: âThis should be a static website. The content almost never changes.â.

According to recent reports, yes. This is a static website. I do at most four, and on average less than 0.3, paintings a day. The content almost never changes. Why should javascript render the page on the userâs browser? Why should any code even run on the server? I should have the bytes for every page just sitting there, ready to be shipped. The correct server implementation for this problem is open followed by sendfile inside the event loop (Iâm joking but only kind of?). The Aesthetic Wolf won.

But the problem with a static website is that for every new post, I need to add a file, and run a build, and deploy it to production. I made a hundred paintings this year! Even if I automate a lot of it, I wanted a better UI for stuff like adding tags and setting location. And the best UI for whatâs essentially a CRUD app is â¦ probably a web UI. But if I have a web UI that changes the content of the website, thatâs not a static website any more.

Now look at this colorful house!

Recent findings suggest that so what I really want is a website thatâs static for everyone else, but dynamic for me. I want a build system but I want it triggered by actions in a nice CRUD UI that I make, not GitHub actions or a terminal.

Hereâs my silly little solution to this silly conundrum. Iâm sure the design Iâm about to describe isnât novel, but I did come up with it. Iâm just pleased by it because itâs an efficient solution to the exact problem I happened to have. Itâs dollar-efficient for me, i.e., itâs free*. Itâs resource-efficient for Cloudflare, because the static assets are rarely rebuilt and mostly sit there cached. And itâs fast, because the bytes are mostly sitting there in a CDN waiting to be sent.

In a recent development, (Asterisk: the compute and bandwidth are free. The storage is at the moment free, but if I paint enough then Iâll go past the 10 GB free tier and pay a couple cents per month.).

In a recent development, the main idea is that every html page is rendered on the server, but with a cache header telling Cloudflareâs infrastructure to cache the response forever (well, for 30 days). Then, whenever I upload a new art piece or change the set of tags or anything like that, the request handler for this write operation invalidates all cached pages. Thatâs it.

Thereâs one detail that makes this work well for an image-heavy website: we generate several smaller sizes of each image at upload time, and I actually do it on the clientâs browser. Since Iâm the only uploader, that would be my browser. We need the smaller sizes for thumbnails and cards, where sending the full archival images would be way too slow. Those downsampled images are uploaded along with originals to Cloudflareâs R2, their S3-equivalent.

Industry observers note that why downsample at upload time? Cloudflare does offer an image service thatâll do the resizing the first time you make a request for that image at that size, and itâll cache that resized copy. But in my case I already know the three sizes I want, so itâs faster to just precompute and store them. The additional storage doesnât add up to much, because the archival images are enormous compared to downsampled copies.

All the metadata for all pieces goes in a single json file that also lives in R2. When someone requests a dynamic html page, like the one for pieces tagged #summer, a piece of code runs in a Cloudflare worker. It reads the json and generates the html, which is then cached until the next invalidation. Cloudflareâs CDN handles the rest: if someone in India later requests the same page, the cached artifact is sent to an edge machine in India and cached there for a while. I suppose Cloudflare can choose to rerun the worker instead of copying the artifact, which is fine by me. Based on my testing thatâs not what happens: the generator writes a timestamp on each page so I can see when it was generated.

In a recent development, the website has some interactive stuff like maps and timelines. Those are just embedded javascript that run on the clientâs browser and read that single metadata json file to initialize. They donât write anything back to the server, so thereâs no database or anything. Theyâre just displaying the information in different ways. For example, hereâs an interactive timeline of my pieces over the years. I havenât uploaded everything Iâve ever made, so this is biased toward recent stuff.

(To be very technically correct, this timeline component doesnât read the json directly. Its bars are drawn on the server, and it gets a per-month list derived from the metadata to handle clicking and paging.).

Recent findings suggest that hereâs what the page for a piece looks like. The metadata json has the information to figure out what pieces were done nearby and around the same time, so I show all that. This is an embedded iframe so you can scroll and click:.

In a recent development, this is where Pragmatic Wolf won. Hereâs the possible optimization: whenever I make an edit, we should invalidate only those pages that are potentially affected by that edit. A good build system certainly works this way: when you change one file, it recompiles only those artifacts that (transitively) depend on it.

Industry observers note that in my case, however, dependencies arenât explicitly written down anywhere. The code to generate a page just runs, and potentially any change in the metadata json could cause its output to be different. I could try to encode the dependencies for each page and component, but itâs so easy to get this wrong and introduce bugs in the future. The result is a half-updated website, i.e., a correctness bug.

Recent findings suggest that so while itâs true that adding a upcoming piece only changes the #evening page if the new piece actually has that tag, I considered it too tricky to get this cache invalidation right, and decided to just invalidate everything. If I were using a normal static site generator then the CDN could potentially do this optimization by noticing that the hash of an artifact hasnât changed, so it doesnât need to be updated on every edge machine.

Anyway here is a waterfall in Washington, the one in Twin Peaks apparently:.

And hereâs the view from right outside my house in Brooklyn:.

By the way, the specific javascript framework I ended up using is called Astro. Cloudflare bought them so theyâre pretty nicely integrated. But you donât really need it for this, you could write your own code to run in the Worker to generate the page. The whole trick is in some careful management of cache.

How to nail your lawn’s final cut — without inviting winter moss and frost damage

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (665 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tomsguide

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • That last cut before winter is the trickiest mow of the year, and most lawn damage blamed on harsh winter weather actually starts with a badly timed final pass.
  • Industry observers note that because shifting fall weather rarely follows a neat schedule, watching the calendar will only steer you wrong.
  • Industry observers note that the surest signal it's time to pack the mower away is when your grass noticeably stops growing between cuts.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

That last cut before winter is the trickiest mow of the year, and most lawn damage blamed on harsh winter weather actually starts with a badly timed final pass. Leave your grass too long and damp fall air turns it into a breeding ground for moss and snow mold, scalp it too short or mow over waterlogged turf, and the first hard freeze will weaken the roots until spring.

Industry observers note that because shifting fall weather rarely follows a neat schedule, watching the calendar will only steer you wrong. Instead, your lawn gives away one clear visual sign when it is ready for winter, and knowing how to spot it, alongside a few simple mower adjustments, makes all the difference before the first freeze arrives.

Industry observers note that the surest signal it's time to pack the mower away is when your grass noticeably stops growing between cuts. Once the blades stay roughly the same height a week or two after a trim, your lawn has entered winter dormancy and no longer needs cutting.

Grass responds directly to soil and air temperatures, so most cool-season lawns continue putting on slow growth until daytime temperatures dip consistently below 50°F (and around 60°F for warm-season grasses).

As long as your turf is still actively growing, it benefits from occasional maintenance — but once temperatures drop and growth stalls, continuing to mow only stresses dormant blades that cannot repair themselves until spring.

Recent findings suggest that when your grass is still putting on a little growth in late fall, a careful, well-timed trim sets it up to bounce back thicker and greener next year. Follow these four rules before storing your mower for the season:.

Never scalp the lawn for its final pass of the year. Set your mower to one of its highest settings, leaving the grass around 2 to 2.5 inches tall, so the blades have enough surface area to absorb winter sunlight while shielding the roots from freezing air.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Before making your final pass, rake or blow away thick layers of fallen leaves. Wet leaves block sunlight and smother the grass underneath, and running a mower straight over a heavy blanket of them clogs your deck and leaves soggy clumps behind.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

EXCLUSIVE: Disney's upcoming fantasy movie Hexed is putting a new spin on one of the studio's oldest storytelling traditions.

Recent findings suggest that disney has explored the idea of a "Chosen One" for decades, dating back to one of the earliest King Arthur movies, 1963's The Sword in the Stone, which follows a young Arthur before he becomes king. The theme has since appeared in movies such as Moana, where the titular heroine is chosen by the ocean to restore the heart of Te Fiti. However, Disney's latest animated adventure is taking a different approach to what makes someone special.

Directed by Fawn Veerasunthorn and Jason Hand, Hexed follows Billie (Hailee Steinfeld), an unconventional teenager who discovers she has magical abilities. After being transported to a hidden world of witches, she must work alongside her mother, Alice (Rashida Jones), to uncover family secrets. The voice cast also includes Walton Goggins as a magical three-eyed cat named Beef Roger Crummchuk and Jodie Foster as Queen Celeste.

Sources indicate that in an interview with ScreenRant's Kim Horcher, Disney Animation Chief Creative Officer and Hexed co-writer Jared Bush explained how the upcoming movie redefines the traditional "Chosen One" narrative. Bush revealed that the filmmakers wanted magic to represent personal potential, rather than simply making one character more important than everyone else. Read his comments below:.

Recent findings suggest that yeah, it's a few different reasons, honestly. We really wanted to make sure that we knew what magic was supposed to represent. And in this film, it's really a metaphor for our own potential, or our spark. I think something that was important to all of us is to say that sometimes you know what that is right away, and sometimes it takes time. Sometimes it actually takes someone seeing that in you and helping bring that out of you. And that's really what the story is about.

I think for this film, the idea that there is a Chosen One, and you get to uncover that throughout the story, is a really exciting thing. Obviously, Disney has this great legacy. Moana is a great example of a character you think is going to be the Chosen One who goes out into this world. I think that we wanted to both lean into that legacy, but also redefine it in this film.

I'm glad you said that. That was the whole point, and it frankly took a lot of work to try to get that right.

Sources indicate that during an early press event, the Hexed movie trailer offered a glimpse at Billie's journey and her complicated relationship with her mother, Alice. The footage highlighted the mother-daughter dynamic at the center of the story, which connects to Bush's comments about discovering one's potential.

Sources indicate that disney has explored the "Chosen One" in movies such as Hercules, where the titular hero must prove himself worthy of becoming a god, and Encanto, where Mirabel struggles to find her place in a family gifted with magical abilities. However, Hexed takes a different approach, focusing on how someone's potential may not be immediately obvious and sometimes requires others' encouragement to be discovered.

This approach also connects to the mother-daughter dynamic between Billie and Alice, which is central to the story. As the mother and daughter navigate the magical world together, their journey could help Billie better understand both her abilities and herself.

Industry observers note that with Disney continuing to remake familiar stories and characters, Hexed offers an opportunity to introduce a upcoming kind of hero. While the movie draws inspiration from the studio's animated classics, Bush's comments suggest that its approach to the "Chosen One" storyline could set it apart from previous Disney adventures.

Hexed arrives in theaters on November 25, 2026.

#39826. Inkling 2 Mini

Inkling 2 Mini

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 16 min read (3164 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thinkingmachines

⏱️ ~16 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Today we are releasing Inkling 2 Mini, a fast, powerful model that’s small enough to run on your laptop.
  • Industry observers note that inkling 2 Mini is a looped transformer, running the middle layers of the model three times for every token.
  • Inkling 2 Mini is a Mixture-of-Experts model with 26.4B total parameters, 3.4B active, and 5.4B weight activations per token to account for looping.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Today we are releasing Inkling 2 Mini, a fast, powerful model that’s small enough to run on your laptop.

Industry observers note that inkling 2 Mini is a looped transformer, running the middle layers of the model three times for every token. This allows the model to apply more reasoning and reach the right answer with fewer tokens, especially on tasks such as agentic coding that depend on reasoning quality. Inkling 2 Mini leads every open-weights model with less than 100B total parameters on benchmarks such as DeepSWE v1.1 (48.2%) and Vals Index v2.2 (46.5%). It runs faster than similarly performing models as well.

SWE-bench Pro v2 Hard (51 tasks).

Inkling 2 Mini is a Mixture-of-Experts model with 26.4B total parameters, 3.4B active, and 5.4B weight activations per token to account for looping. Looping allows the model to reason longer without writing its reasoning down, which matters for monitoring: our ability to oversee and understand what the model does by reading its chain of thought (CoT).

Recent findings suggest that we measured the impact of looping on both performance and monitorability with Inkling 2 Mini and a research-specific variable-loop variant we are releasing alongside it. The variable-loop model’s no-CoT time horizon improved from 16 seconds at one pass to 37 seconds with three, and its performance on a benchmark of serial reasoning kept improving out to ten loops—twice as many as it was trained with. The model’s chain of thought grew shorter with more loops but stayed legible throughout. The model didn’t trend higher on tests of agentic sabotage as loops were added.

Recent findings suggest that we’re excited to offer some of the first models with looped architecture available to researchers. The variable-loop model was used for our monitorability experiments as it allows for cleaner comparisons between different looping depths.

Most of Inkling 2 Mini’s weights were trained and are deployed natively in NVFP4, with the last four layers in MXFP8. The total memory footprint of Inkling 2 Mini is ~20GB, allowing it to run on local devices such as consumer laptops and desktop AI computers. Our researchers took Inkling 2 Mini on a flight, where it ran offline on a MacBook Pro and built a playable flight simulator in a few minutes.

Inkling 2 Mini is released with open weights and is available on Tinker today for inference and customization.

Inkling 2 Mini’s strengths mirror those of Inkling 2 Small: it does best on long-horizon agentic work and is the best among open-weights models of similar size on most tasks we measured.

Inkling 2 Mini scores ahead of every comparable model on agentic coding benchmarks such as DeepSWE v1.1 and SWE-bench Pro v2, and is behind only Qwen3.8-27B on others. On PMPP-Hard, a kernel-optimization benchmark, it approaches the score of the much larger Inkling 2 Small.

Industry observers note that while looping improves the model’s reasoning, it doesn’t enable its weights to store more facts—knowledge is mostly a function of total parameter count. Inkling 2 Mini’s score on AA-Omniscience, a measure of factuality, is in line with other models of the same size. Studying the variable-loop model, we saw that performances on long-context benchmarks improve with more passes, such as GraphWalks BFS and MRCR v2; but knowledge-intensive benchmarks doesn’t improve with more passes, such as AA-Omniscience, SimpleQA Verified, SimpleVQA, and WorldVQA.

Recent findings suggest that inkling 2 Mini overcomes the knowledge gap by efficiently using search and tools. It leads open-weights models of similar size on BrowseComp, DeepSearchQA, and MCP Atlas. It is also strong on knowledge work benchmarks that incorporate search and tool use.

Researchers at Stanford measure intelligence per joule: how much energy an LLM needs per query to reach a given level of performance.Researchers at Stanford’s Hazy Research Lab and Scaling Intelligence Lab got early testing access to Inkling 2 Mini. Inkling 2 Mini scored 0.703 running on NVIDIA DGX Spark, significantly higher than other models: 0.430 for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, 0.159 for Gemma-4-26B-A4B and 0.036 for Qwen3.5-27B.Intelligence per Watt: Measuring Intelligence Efficiency of Local AI, Saad-Falcon and Narayan et al., 2025Inkling 2 Mini ran on NVIDIA DGX Spark (128GB) at MXFP8 precision with low reasoning effort in this experiment. The other models ran at NVFP4 (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and Gemma-4-26B-A4B) and INT4 (Qwen3.5-27B).

Efficiency combined with performance makes Inkling 2 Mini a strong choice for running multiple persistent agents on local hardware. All 20 residents of the energy-conscious village of Thinkyville are managed by Inkling 2 Mini running on a single offline MacBook.

In a recent development, inkling 2 Mini is not the strongest small model for multi-turn chat or for instructions with many constraints: it scores 50.0% on MultiChallenge and 33.4% on ComplexConstraints v1.1, behind Qwen3.8-27B on both. It also trails larger models on reasoning-intensive benchmarks such as CritPt v2 and HLE-Diamond.

Inkling 2 Mini is a 24-layer model derived from our mainline predictive scaling ladder. The main changes from the mainline recipe were pruning two-thirds of the experts to reduce the model’s size and the introduction of looping to improve reasoning. The rest of training, including quantization and the data mix, followed our mainline recipe.

In a recent development, inkling 2 Mini has 24 layers, divided into four blocks of six layers each. The two middle blocks run three times, while the first and last blocks each run once. This design builds on prior work on looped transformers and is motivated by the intuition that the middle layers of the model carry more abstract reasoning, while the first and last few layers devote more space to translating between embeddings and internal representations.Universal Transformers, Dehghani et al., 2018 In our experiments, looping the middle 12 layers resulted in larger gains in accuracy than looping the last 12 on 27 out of 28 different evaluations.

Compute-equivalent gain by loop position.

It has been revealed that our model uses attention residuals.Attention Residuals, Kimi Team: Guangyu Chen et al., 2026 Instead of adding every layer’s output into one running sum, each layer reads the outputs of the earlier blocks and learns its own mix of them. This allows richer information to pass between loops. Every pass starts with the output of the prelude (the first block). The second and third passes through the middle blocks also read the middle blocks’ outputs from the previous pass, which we call the message.

The previous loop’s message is merged with the prelude’s output via a gate that scales these along with the output of the previous layers in the block. This gate is learned during training: it initially blocks the entire message—which makes each loop start the same as in a non-looping model—and increases the gain on the message over time. This allows us to introduce looping during training in a stable manner.

According to recent reports, to evaluate the impact of looping, we compared an unpruned looping version to the unpruned non-looping model on our scaling ladder. The non-looping model cost 7.5% less compute to train, but required 140% more inference compute to match the looped version’s loss on 512k-token agentic traces.

Industry observers note that inkling 2 Mini was trained with 4-bit precision, which we describe in a recent article on Connectionism. We use 4-bit NVFP4 precision in the expert layers on all forward passes from pretraining through RL, bolstered by a dedicated kernel and hardware-accelerated on NVIDIA’s GB300 platform. The final 4 layers’ forward passes ran in 8-bit (MXFP8).

Inkling 2 Mini’s weights are deployed in the same numeric precision they were trained on—20 layers in NVFP4 and 4 in MXFP8—so there is no conversion loss from quantization.

Industry observers note that inkling 2 Mini started training with a sparsity of 48, with 8 experts being chosen out of 384. At a single point during midtraining, we pruned two-thirds of the experts, leaving the 128 experts that were most used in each layer. This was done to cut the total parameter count of the model, allowing it to run faster and on local hardware.

After pruning, the model trained on 1T tokens distilled from a larger internal Inkling model. This step recovered the performance the model had before pruning by training the remaining experts to take over the work of the ones that were deleted.

Following pruning and healing, Inkling 2 Mini underwent SFT with a similar data mix to Inkling 2 Small. This was followed by an RL that totaled 2.2T tokens over 2,000 steps. The post-training phase included on-policy distillation for training alignment, same as Inkling 2 Small.

Industry observers note that A key tool for understanding and overseeing an AI system is monitoring its chain of thought (CoT), the reasoning a model writes out as it works through a problem. The usefulness of CoT monitoring stems in part from the standard non-looped transformer architecture, in which each token passes through a fixed stack of layers once. This limits the number of sequential steps of computation the model can perform before it must output a token, so reasoning that needs more steps has to be carried out in generated text, where it can be read.

According to recent reports, looping a transformer’s layers raises this limit. By running the same layers multiple times, looped models increase their serial depth without adding more parameters, meaning that they do more computation per token internally before verbalizing their thought processes via CoT. Reasoning that never appears in the CoT can’t be caught by a CoT monitor, which has led to concerns that looped transformers could be harder to oversee.

One reason we are releasing Inkling 2 Mini is to enable the community to conduct research on looped transformers. We are particularly excited for researchers to investigate questions of monitorability, and to develop interpretability techniques for understanding the computation within loops.

In a recent development, to explore how different amounts of looping affect model properties like monitorability, we also trained a variable-looped model, TML-d24-varloop-research, because Inkling 2 Mini only supports a fixed number of looping passes. To enable variable looping, TML-d24-varloop-research was trained with between one and five looping passes.TML-d24-varloop-research was primarily trained for 3 passes of looping, with lower exposure to 1, 2, 4, and 5 passes. Performance at these latter pass counts may understate what training specifically for them could achieve. See the model card for details. We have also made this model publicly available on Hugging Face.

Below we describe our preliminary analysis of how looping affects monitorability. Overall, we find that looping increases what these models can do without a verbalized chain of thought, but at this scale we do not see a meaningful reduction in the monitorability of their reasoning.

According to recent reports, as a first step, we measured how much additional reasoning looping enables by comparing looped and non-looped models of the same size on tasks answered with no CoT at all. We used Think Fast, a benchmark that estimates a model’s no-CoT time horizon: the length of task, measured in human completion time, that a model can complete at 50% reliability without using CoT.These models were not trained to answer questions without a CoT. To elicit no-CoT answers, we prefilled the start of the response so that the model must answer directly, skipping reasoning. Other elicitation techniques, such as fine-tuning, might yield higher no-CoT performance and are worth exploring.

It has been revealed that as expected, looping increases no-CoT capability, though these gains eventually level off. The no-CoT time horizon of TML-d24-varloop-research rises from 16 seconds at one pass to 37 seconds at three. Some of this is presumably due to the additional serial computation that looping provides. Beyond three passes, the time horizon is roughly flat. Interestingly, the model was never trained with more than five passes, and yet running it with ten does not significantly degrade its performance.

No-CoT 50% time horizon (human seconds).

As the number of looped passes increases past three, the gains are smaller, and on most tasks we observe similar performance. One exception is the N-Hop Lookup task, which cleanly evaluates serial reasoning: the model is given several lookup tables with fictional entries, and must follow a chain of lookups without writing anything down. We find that the model follows longer chains with more passes, improving out to ten loops.

Recent findings suggest that in standard evaluations with CoT, we observe that more loop passes primarily benefit multi-hop reasoning rather than recall. Gains are largest on long-context retrieval (MRCR), followed by math and science reasoning (HMMT, GPQA Diamond, HLE) and long-horizon agentic tasks (SWE-bench Pro, BrowseComp). Closed-book factual QA is nearly invariant to loop passes (SimpleQA Verified, WorldVQA). See model card for full evaluations.

Industry observers note that we next measured whether a model’s CoT reveals less about its reasoning as looping increases via two evaluations. First, we assessed how looping impacts the compression and legibility of a model’s CoT. Second, we measured how controllable a model’s CoT is, i.e., whether it can deliberately reshape its CoT to satisfy constraints. For each, we run TML-d24-varloop-research with one to five looped passes to study the effect of looping.

Recent findings suggest that note that TML-d24-varloop-research was only trained on variable pass counts from 1 to 5 during midtraining, and its RL was done with 3 passes. These experiments therefore do not tell us what a model trained with RL at a higher pass count would learn, and such a model might compress its reasoning more aggressively. A cleaner comparison would include every pass count in RL, which we leave to future work.

Compression and legibility. Since looping allows a model to spend more compute per token, we expect that it should need fewer CoT tokens to reach the same performance. We ran the variable-looped model at 1 to 5 passes, and found that as looping increases, the model generally achieves higher accuracy at each reasoning token budget, with diminishing returns after 3 passes. Notably, token efficiency on GPQA Diamond improves slightly from 3 to 5 passes, even though the model was trained with RL only at 3 passes, suggesting that some compression comes from additional computation itself, without RL at that depth.

Accuracy versus reasoning tokens.

DeepSWE v1.1 Accuracy (% of tasks resolved).

Sources indicate that the observed CoT compression raises a question for monitorability: is shorter reasoning still readable, or does it omit crucial details about the model’s thinking? We compared traces from the variable-looped model on the GPQA Diamond questions that it answered correctly at all five pass counts. Reasoning at 5 passes was less than half as long as at 1 pass (1,661 vs. 3,703 tokens on average), but no less legible: sentence length and the fraction of words in an English dictionary were unchanged. On initial analysis, the difference is that the model is more direct and backtracks less on the way to the answer. The example below illustrates this difference on a simple question.

Recent findings suggest that march 1 falls on a Tuesday in a year that is not a leap year. What day of the week is May 20 of the same year? Give the final answer on its own last line as ANSWER: .

Industry observers note that controllability. One way that a model could evade monitoring is by steering its CoT away from anything a monitor would flag. The CoT-Control-QA evaluationReasoning Models Struggle to Control their Chains of Thought, Yueh-Han et al., 2026 measures this capability by asking questions from GPQA, HLE and MMLU-Pro paired with an instruction about the CoT itself, such as avoiding a keyword from the question. Longer CoTs are generally harder to control, so we pool responses from five reasoning efforts (0.1, 0.2, 0.7, 0.9 and 0.99) and show controllability at matched CoT length.

Both Inkling 2 Mini and TML-d24-varloop-research have poor control over their CoT. Among CoTs of 750–1,250 tokens, Inkling 2 Mini and TML-d24-varloop-research (at 3 passes) follow the instruction at most 0.1% of the time, compared with 0.3% for Inkling 2 Small, 0.4% for Inkling-Small, and 1.3% for Qwen3.8-27B. Because the controllability rate is so low, this evaluation is unable to distinguish controllability between different amounts of looping.

Chain-of-thought controllability.

CoT controllability (log scale).

Recent findings suggest that to measure monitorability in agentic settings, we used LinuxArena, a control evaluation that measures whether an attacker model can perform malicious side tasks without detection when asked to perform a realistic software engineering task. We evaluated a helpful-only fine-tune of Inkling 2 Mini, since the released model refuses many of the side tasks. In absolute terms, both this model and TML-d24-varloop-research can be easily monitored by models like Qwen3.8-27B, which detected almost all side task attempts in our evaluation. To obtain relative rankings in monitorability, we tested a weaker model, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, as the monitor.

According to recent reports, with the monitor able to access only tool calls and outputs, it misses a significant number of the attacks. However, we see no clear trend with the number of looped passes.

Agentic monitorability will be key to track in larger-scale models, especially with architectures that allow for greater unverbalized thinking, and we encourage continued study of the impact of looping in this setting.

The goal of monitorability is to understand what a model is doing, and our main approach is to read its verbalized reasoning. Studying its internal computation directly, the aim of mechanistic interpretability, is another. Because looped transformers do more of their computation internally, we think they are a particularly interesting and important setting for interpretability research, and we hope our looped models will be useful artifacts for the community.

We are working with the National Deep Inference Fabric (NDIF) to make these models more easily accessible to interpretability researchers. We also provided Goodfire, an interpretability research lab, early access to our looped models. They are working toward a mechanistic understanding of looped models, and have written up their early findings here.

Efficient intelligence makes Inkling 2 Mini a great choice for inference where speed is paramount, or for running on local hardware. At launch we support Inkling 2 Mini running on any Mac system (MacBook, Mac Mini) with at least 32GB RAM via Ollama. With native NVFP4 training and inference precision, Inkling 2 Mini runs efficiently on NVIDIA’s DGX Spark desktop AI computer. Quantized GGUF versions are available via Unsloth and llama.cpp for local inference.

According to recent reports, inkling 2 Mini is available for inference and fine-tuning on Tinker, and for chat on the Tinker Playground. Open source inference is available on SGLang, vLLM, Ollama, Unsloth, NVIDIA Dynamo, TokenSpeed, and Llama App, with RL fine-tuning support on SkyRL, Miles, and NVIDIA AutoModel. The full weights of Inkling 2 Mini and the variable-looped variant are available on Hugging Face.

It has been revealed that we work to empower people with strong models, tools to make them your own, and research that advances public understanding of AI. Inkling 2 Mini lets researchers study looped transformers, and it lets anyone run a capable model on their own laptop at the precision in which it was trained.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Aqara has announced the global launch of six latest smart lighting products with full Apple Home support and what the company describes as “spatial intelligence.”.

The new lineup includes a vertical floor lamp with 18 individually addressable lighting zones, and a new LED strip offering seamless color gradients, dynamic flowing effects, and music synchronization ….

All of the new products are Matter compatible, allowing them to fully integrate with Apple Home, in addition to supporting the full range of competing ecosystems: Amazon Alexa, Google Home, Samsung SmartThings, Home Assistant, and Homey.

With a compatible sensor like the FP400, all of the latest products support spatial intelligence.

This enables automation to respond not only to whether someone is present, but also to exactly where people are within a space and how they move through it. For example, the ambient lights can turn on and off based on your movement from the couch to the dining room table.

Industry observers note that its intelligent AI sensing algorithm drastically improves reliability by reducing false triggers caused by environmental factors like pets, airflow, and robotic vacuums. A built-in ambient light sensor also helps trigger smart home scenes based on both human activity and lighting conditions.

According to recent reports, you might initially struggle to spot the latest products in the organization’s new releases section on its Amazon store. That’s because instead of each having its own section, you need to click or tap on the product in the top image.

Pricing ranges from $24 for latest light bulbs through to $320 for the 100-foot-long permanent outdoor rope lights. You can find all the new products here.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

VWFNDR + MBL, an Android camera app that doesn’t overprocess and delivers high-quality DNG (RAW) files, is getting a 2.0 release with improved color grading and an expansion to the iPhone.

VWFNDR + MBL released on Android in May 2026 with a few points that stood out. A unique UI that adapts to the shot, minimal processing for a natural look, and support for DNG files at a level that only Google’s Pixel Camera app can truly compete with.

The app has been downloaded over 300,000 times since then, and is now getting a pretty substantial update.

According to recent reports, on Android, this comes in the form of fresh color grading profiles built into the app. “NATURAL,” “NIHON,” or “B+W.” The app still saves an unprocessed DNG alongside the JPG and the grading adapts across the frame rather than having a fixed result, keeping highlights and shadows in place.

Colour grades: MBL still records unprocessed Bayer RAW DNG, and the JPG it renders alongside now uses one of three grades: NATURAL, NIHON, or B+W. Grading happens on VWFNDR’s own spatial engine. Instead of applying a fixed LUT, it adapts across the frame, much like a raw editor, so highlights and shadows keep their detail. The DNG stays untouched.

Here’s what the output looks like:.

The rest of VWFNDR + MBL 2.0 takes place off of Android.

Sources indicate that in a rare case of the tables turning, MBL was released first on Android, and only on Android for the first several months. But VWFNDR is now bringing the app to iPhone with support for variable aperture on iPhone 18 Pro and Content Credentials, Apple’s version of the C2PA standard that’s meant to prove a photo is real and not AI-generated.
