Ridley Scott's Involvement In Latest Blade Runner Series Clarified By Showrunner & EPs

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (479 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Screenrant

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ahead of Blade Runner 2099's official release, executive producers Silka Louisa and Broderick Johnson revealed the extent to which franchise creator Ridley Scott was involved with the Prime Video series.
  • Set 50 years after Blade Runner 2049, the show stars Hunter Schafer as Cora, a human pretending to be a replicant, and Michelle Yeoh as Olwen, an aging replicant, in a world where replicants are dominant over humans.
  • Sources indicate that in an interview with Maude Garrett for ScreenRant, the Blade Runner 2099 executive producers addressed working with Scott on one of his most iconic properties.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ahead of Blade Runner 2099's official release, executive producers Silka Louisa and Broderick Johnson revealed the extent to which franchise creator Ridley Scott was involved with the Prime Video series.

Set 50 years after Blade Runner 2049, the show stars Hunter Schafer as Cora, a human pretending to be a replicant, and Michelle Yeoh as Olwen, an aging replicant, in a world where replicants are dominant over humans. The rest of the cast is rounded out by Dimitri Abold and Lewis Gribben.

Sources indicate that in an interview with Maude Garrett for ScreenRant, the Blade Runner 2099 executive producers addressed working with Scott on one of his most iconic properties. "It's a dream come true to know all of the secrets and ask him all the questions and find out what everything really means," Louisa said.

Recent findings suggest that however, she clarify that some secrets have to stay close to her chest. "The one thing I don't tell anyone because, I will warn you, you think you want to know, but you don't want to know," the writer explained. "The power of never really being sure, the ambiguity is that, is so tantalizing. And somebody actually just telling you definitively, "It's X, it's Y..." It just kind of neuters the magic trick." A key factor in Blade Runner's appeal over the decades has been its ambiguity over whether Rick Deckard (portrayed by Harrison Ford in Scott's Blade Runner) is himself a replicant, a question Louisa sidesteps because "everyone tries" to get a solid answer from her.

Sources indicate that for Johnson, his working relationship with Scott goes back "now a good 15 years," and he still recalls the open attitude the filmmaker had to expanding the world of Blade Runner. "When we first got the IP and went and sat with him," said Johnson. "He told us in that first meeting that Blade Runner was never meant to be a one-off exercise, which we were thrilled to hear. That collaboration has gone on since then.".

According to Johnson, Scott's collaborative approach very much extended to Louisa's vision for Blade Runner 2099. "He responded to Silka's original idea very positively as well," he continued. "He's been a part of that iteration from the [start], deciding whether it's a hundred years or it's 50 years or whatever. He was part of that whole thing, dreaming with her at that point, down to giving notes on the edits and whatnot.".

Scott himself previously discussed his involvement with the series, somewhat contradicting the assertion he was heavily involved. "I can’t blame my lawyers and my agents at that time, but somehow we let ‘Blade Runner’ go," he noted earlier this year. "And when you’re not the author of the actual written word, you don’t have a piece.".

Blade Runner 2099 debuts on Prime Video on November 25, 2026.

The 8 Most Challenging Books To Read That Are 100% Worth It

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1491 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Collider

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that many things can make a book challenging to read.
  • From foundational classics like In Search of Lost Time to modern award-winning masterpieces like Angel Down, these are books which are certainly challenging to get through, but are so phenomenal that they are 100% worth the challenge.
  • In a recent development, french novelist, essayist, and literary critic Marvel Proust was one of the most influential authors of the entire 20th century, best-known for his seven-volume magnum opus In Search of Lost Time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that many things can make a book challenging to read. Perhaps it's because their use of language is deliberately labyrinthine or jargon-heavy, because their narrative structure feels almost surreal, or because a lot of background knowledge is required to fully understand the story. In any case, there have been innumerable great-yet-difficult books written over the years, and it just so happens that quite a few of them are among the best books ever written.

From foundational classics like In Search of Lost Time to modern award-winning masterpieces like Angel Down, these are books which are certainly challenging to get through, but are so phenomenal that they are 100% worth the challenge. For the purposes of this list, only books that were specifically designed to be challenging will be considered, rather than great books that are hard to read today mostly because they have dated aspects, which is a whole other topic. The entries are ranked by a mixture of how essential and how challenging each book is.

In a recent development, french novelist, essayist, and literary critic Marvel Proust was one of the most influential authors of the entire 20th century, best-known for his seven-volume magnum opus In Search of Lost Time. Published between 1913 and 1927, the novel is composed of a narrator's recollections of his childhood and journey to adulthood, revisiting his past, romantic obsessions, and relationships with French high society as he tries to find his purpose as a writer.

According to recent reports, the main reason why In Search of Lost Time is such a challenging read goes without saying. Depending on what format one reads it in, the novel is over 4,000 pages and 1.2 million words long. It's a kind of literary Everest that many a bibliophile considers a true goal to climb to the top, and far from being a tedious journey that's mostly worth reading just because it's a classic, it's a genuinely phenomenal work of art of tremendous psychological depth and gorgeous prose.

According to recent reports, toni Morrison's Beloved is one of those books that everyone should read before kicking the bucket, one of the most consequential American novels of the 20th century. It tells the story of a formerly enslaved mother in post-Civil War Ohio, as she's haunted by the ghost of the baby she killed to spare her from slavery. The book won the 1988 Pulitzer Prize for Fiction and is still widely remembered as one of the most foundational texts for postcolonial, African American, and feminist literature.

Sources indicate that on the one hand, you have the book's brutally harrowing subject matter, which Morrison dives deep into without flinching at any point. On top of that, you get the highly fragmented, non-linear storytelling, as well as Morrison's dense and poetic prose. But though it isn't an easy read, Beloved is absolutely breathtaking, a book whose historical importance is matched only by its artistic quality.

Though the world of Latin American literature hasn't been quite as internationally mainstream throughout the 21st century as it was during the '60s and '70s, it has nonetheless delivered several incredible masterpieces. Case in point: Chilean writer Roberto Bolaño's postmodern meta-novel 2666, a gut-wrenching tale about four European literary critics searching for an elusive German author. On their journey, they encounter a wave of unsolved femicides in a Mexican border town inspired by Ciudad Juárez.

It has been revealed that 2666 is nothing but relentless surrealist cruelty over a whopping 900 pages, easily making it one of the heaviest books of all time. Reading it requires not only deciphering its sprawling, fragmented structure, but also bearing such a devastatingly realistic depiction of violence toward women in Mexico and Latin America that getting to the end of the novel is already an achievement in itself. But far from feeling exploitative, 2666 is propelled by Bolaño's hypnotic prose and unforgettable characters, making all of the bleakness worth every word.

Legendary postmodernist icon Thomas Pynchon was well-known for writing some of the densest, most complex and challenging novels of the entire postmodern movement, such as the satirical historical sci-fi masterpiece Gravity's Rainbow. It's one of the heaviest sci-fi books ever written, about an American soldier fighting in Europe during World War II. There, he discovers that his sexual encounters map onto future German rocket strikes, launching a paranoid quest into a secret conspiracy.

Recent findings suggest that generally considered Pynchon's most deliberately challenging novel, Gravity's Rainbow stands as a total refusal of traditional ideas of narrative. There's no conventional plot, no real character arc, no linear time; instead, the whole book is overloaded with theology, history, economics, pop culture references, and labyrinthine language. Even so, Gravity's Rainbow is a must-read for people already familiar with Pynchon's style, since it very well may be the quintessential countercultural epic.

Plenty of great books have won the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction throughout the 2020s, and Daniel Kraus' Angel Down is one of the best. In it, World War I soldiers venture into No Man's Land to put a wounded comrade out of his misery, only to find a fallen angel whose fate plants greed, paranoia, and moral ruin in their midst. It already seems like a compelling enough premise on paper, but what really makes Angel Down so special—and so challenging—is that the whole thing is a single unbroken sentence.

Recent findings suggest that making a single sentence span a whopping 300 pages was always going to be a gargantuan task to complete successfully, but Angel Down really does live up to the hype. Yes, the complete lack of breaks in the book is mentally draining, but it's worth every bit of effort it demands. Angel Down is a deeply moving and thought-provoking study of the existential horrors of war, blending visceral supernatural horror and war thriller genre elements faultlessly.

One of the most vital and influential American writers of his generation, William Faulkner is still considered one of the spearheads of 20th-century Southern American literature and modernist fiction. In his fourth-ever novel, he delivered his magnum opus. The Sound and the Fury chronicles the collapse of an aristocratic Mississippi family as three brothers' obsessions with their sister unravel across fragmented, shifting perspectives.

Recent findings suggest that the result of such a premise is one of those perfect books that immediately demand a re-read, and that speaks both to this masterpiece's tremendous quality and highly challenging stream-of-consciousness style. The Sound and the Fury feels like one of the most successful experiments that modernist fiction ever gave us, shifting through several different perspectives that make the whole reading experience feel like a psychological maze. Getting through it, however, delivers one of the most foundational masterpieces of early-20th-century American literature.

Industry observers note that "Newly introduced sincerity" was a trend in late-20th-century art that sought to break away from postmodernism's sense of irony and cynicism, in relation to the post-postmodern cultural paradigm of metamodernism. As far as those concepts go, you can't really get many exponents much better than David Foster Wallace's magnum opus, Infinite Jest. Cataloged as an encyclopedic novel, it's set in a near-future North America where Quebec separatists, intelligence agents, tennis prodigies, and recovering addicts collide in a search for a fatally addictive film cartridge created by a late filmmaker.

The result is one of the most ambitious books of all time, a 1,000-page doorstop that serves as a potent statement about addiction, entertainment, isolation, and the endless search for sincere human connection. It's a towering artistic achievement packed with hundreds of endnotes with vital information, a challenging non-linear structure, and hyper-dense prose that makes reading multiple pages at a time all that much harder. However, it's also a brilliantly prophetic satire about entertainment and the media, full of hilarious set pieces and intelligent payoffs.

In a recent development, one of the most influential and groundbreaking writers of the 20th century, James Joyce wrote what many would consider a remarkably strong contender for the elusive title of The Great American Novel: Ulysses, one of the classics that belong on everyone's bucket list. This is a modernist mirror of Homer's Odyssey, following an ordinary Dublin advertiser and a young writer through a single day in their ordinary lives. Who could have possibly predicted that a book that simply narrates a mundane day could be so challenging?

According to recent reports, indeed, Joyce completely reinvents the rules that his book operates under with practically every single chapter, writing in an unfiltered stream of consciousness that never holds the reader's hand. Full of dense allusions to things like Catholic theology, Shakespearean scholarship, and Dublin lore, it's certainly not an easy masterpiece to get through, but it's a must-read nonetheless. But as challenging as it is, Ulysses is also the most admirable and humane portrait of an ordinary person ever written as fiction, an absolute masterwork that belongs on the bookshelf of everyone who loves books.

Although it’s rare for the Siri Remote to get firmware updates, Apple pushed out upcoming firmware for the latest Siri Remote just yesterday per AppleDB.

You can’t manually update your Siri Remote’s firmware. But as long as it’s sufficiently charged and connected to your Apple TV, the update will install automatically in the background.

This revision is only available for the latest Siri Remote (4th gen).

If you’re interested in the newly introduced Siri Remote, but don’t want to buy a whole new Apple TV 4K, it’s available here as a $59 purchase and works with all Apple TV 4K and Apple TV HD models.

I haven’t personally encountered any concerns with the latest Siri Remote since getting it last Friday, but apparently Apple discovered a problem that needed fixing.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that apple only released high-end ‘Pro’ and ‘Duo’ iPhones this fall, marking a departure from previous years when more affordable models debuted too. But iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 are still coming, and a new report offers an enhancement on release timing.

A latest report from Kim Yeong-ho at ETNews provides a fresh enhancement on timing for the iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2.

Rumors have indicated for well over a year that Apple planned to push these models out of the typical fall launch window and introduce them in early 2027 instead.

Industry observers note that per ETNews, Samsung and LG are providing the display panels for the latest models, with Samsung the sole supplier for iPhone Air 2 and both companies splitting orders for iPhone 18. And their mass production plans signal a March release for the products.

Kim Yeong-ho, writing at ETNews:.

Samsung Display looks to begin mass production in January, while LG Display will start late this year…The Korean panel makers appear to be aligning their production plans with an expected March launch.

A March launch window lines up well with when Apple tends to ramp up product introductions following a slower winter. Earlier this year, iPhone 17e debuted in March alongside upcoming Macs and the iPad Air.

The year before, however, the iPhone 16e arrived in February instead.

With Apple shaking up its normal iPhone rollout schedule, it was anyone’s guess how soon the new models would debut. But a March launch makes sense and gives Apple a trio of new iPhones every six months—three unveiled in September, and another three in March.

Nora Pacetti figures her daughter is teething. It would explain the screaming, and by bath time, Olivia seems happy enough. There’s still the matter of what looks like a splinter in her arm, though Nora can’t think where a baby would have picked one up. Her mother, Giulia, gets a good look while she’s toweling off her granddaughter and asks Nora to run downstairs for her reading glasses. Of all the things a grandmother might find on a changing table, an incoming feather takes some explaining.

It has been revealed that giulia is usually the person Nora can count on to have whatever a child might need. She carries an ice pack in her purse in case somebody else’s kid takes a fall, and she also spends enough time watching conspiracy videos on YouTube that Nora would like a second opinion on the feather. Her husband is happy to oblige. He wants to take Olivia to a specialist, and under almost any other circumstances, Nora would probably be the one making the appointment. This time, she’s afraid of what might happen once somebody else gets a look at her daughter.

According to recent reports, christina Henry’s Pinfeathers is out now from Berkley. Released November 17, the 320-page thriller is the 20th book from the author of The Place Where They Buried Your Heart. The book has already drawn comparisons to both Rosemary’s Baby and David Cronenberg’s The Fly, with the feathers accounting for the Cronenberg half. The Rosemary’s Baby bit comes into play when people outside the family begin asking questions about Olivia, and Nora has to figure out who told them enough to ask.

Sources indicate that four franchises, four completely different ways of getting underneath your skin. This is the one built out of your particular fear, why it works so well on you, and what it would leave behind.

Sources indicate that your nightmare does not wait outside the door. It waits for you to close your eyes, which you are going to have to do eventually, because nobody has ever won that particular argument.

It has been revealed that your nightmare is not really the doll. It is the face of the person you tell, and the way they decide, very kindly, that you have imagined all of it.

Your nightmare has your number, knows your name, and has almost certainly been inside your house before. The worst part is that you already know them.

Recent findings suggest that your nightmare is not really about you. It is about the people asleep down the hall, and the feeling that whatever is here is not interested in leaving.

Industry observers note that henry told the Chicago Sun-Times that the image of a baby sprouting feathers came to her before she knew the story. She begins her books in longhand and works out what those early images mean as she writes. In this case, that process brought her to a new mother in a condo on Chicago’s North Side. Henry described the fear behind Nora’s story as “the parental anxiety around illness, difficulty, things that you don’t expect when you become a parent.”.

According to recent reports, readers can get a look at the scene that started it all in an excerpt published by The Nerd Daily, which reveals the three generations of Pacetti women in the middle of an otherwise ordinary visit. Giulia shows up with food, kisses her daughter hello, and nudges her out of the way so she can have a turn with the baby. By the time she notices Olivia’s arm, Henry has already established who usually takes charge in this family.

Pinfeathers is available now in hardcover, ebook, and audiobook.

  • In a recent development, face unlock isn’t a full-fledged Face ID, and it doesn’t work for features like Apple Pay, but it is a convenient fresh option for unlocking your iPhone Duo just by looking at it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

iOS 27.3 rolls out next month and includes several exciting changes for iPhone Duo, here’s what’s upcoming for Apple’s foldable model.

Apple is granting iPhone Duo people one of their biggest feature requests: face unlock is coming with iOS 27.3.

In a recent development, face unlock isn’t a full-fledged Face ID, and it doesn’t work for features like Apple Pay, but it is a convenient fresh option for unlocking your iPhone Duo just by looking at it. Per Apple:.

Industry observers note that use the front camera, along with a recent Touch ID or passcode authentication, to quickly unlock iPhone Duo when it’s closed. Face recognition data never leaves your device.

In a recent development, if your iPhone Duo has gone unused for 45 minutes or more, face unlock won’t work and you’ll need to authenticate with Touch ID or your passcode. But for most owners, that probably just means using Touch ID first thing in the morning, then relying on face unlock the rest of the day.

On a related note, you can also enable Attention Aware features in iOS 27.3. These are available whether you use the face unlock feature or not, but are limited to the outer display. Once enabled, they can automatically lower the volume of alarms and timers, keep the display from dimming, and more.

Read more: iOS 27.3 adds fresh face unlock feature for iPhone Duo.

In a recent development, reachability is available on other iPhone models to move onscreen content down vertically, closer to your thumb. But on iPhone Duo with iOS 27.3, Apple has a unique twist on the feature.

Instead of helping you reach content vertically, Reachability on iPhone Duo works horizontally.

If you’re using the outer screen and find that buttons or other UI elements are out of reach, you can swipe from the side to have onscreen content shift closer to your thumb.

In a recent development, you can always disable Reachability if you find yourself accidentally triggering it too often. But if one-handed iPhone Duo use gives you trouble, Reachability is a great latest option to have.

Read more: iOS 27.3 introduces newly introduced iPhone Duo feature for one-handed use.

In a recent development, what should happen when you close your iPhone Duo’s folding screen? Apple has found that users have different preferences. Some want the iPhone to stay unlocked for continued use, while others prefer that it automatically locks when closed.

In iOS 27.3, Apple adds a newly introduced setting so users can enable whichever behavior they prefer.

By default, iPhone Duo will work as it always has, staying unlocked after being closed. But inside Settings ⇾ Display & Brightness, iOS 27.3 provides the option of automatically locking upon being closed instead. You could achieve something similar before with Shortcuts, but now there’s a built-in setting too.

Recent findings suggest that it’s not exactly a “latest feature,” but iPhone Duo consumers will also find that the system keyboard has changed in iOS 27.3. Apple tweaked the outer display keyboard to push keys closer together and make one-handed use easier.

Here’s a comparison of the old and new keyboards via Beta Profiles on X:.

Industry observers note that iOS 27.3 beta tweaks iPhone Duo's outer display keyboard, with narrower keys and a slightly thinner, smaller font. pic.twitter.com/BDKCBZc52Z.

According to recent reports, wally West, a.k.a. The Flash, has been one of DC Comics’ heaviest hitters for decades. Like the other characters who have access to the Speed Force, his super speed is useful for more than just running quickly. Generating vortexes, vibrating through objects, and traveling through time are just a few of the additional powers that Wally has demonstrated on many occasions. On top of that, he’s officially considered the fastest of the Flashes, outpacing predecessors Jay Garrick and Barry Allen.

According to recent reports, as if all this wasn’t enough, Wally has also displayed a fresh precognitive ability in the current volume of The Flash. Over the last few months, the third Flash has used his “flashes of insight” to predict the immediate future and prevent crimes and horrific incidents from happening in the first place. However, Wally’s use of this precognition has drawn concern from his fellow superheroes, and now four of the Justice League are clashing with the Scarlet Speedster to rein him in.

Though he started out with good intentions, Flash has morphed into an anti-hero because of how he’s been using his precognition. Green Arrow took issue with Wally trying to prevent all bad things from happening in Star City after he’d previously done so in Central City and Metropolis, comparing the speedster’s use of this power to fascism. Wally ignored his warnings, and when that caused even more problems, Green Arrow called in some fellow superheroes to help him out with this predicament.

According to recent reports, by the end of The Flash #38, Green Arrow ordered the Justice Leaguers he’d looped in to “take The Flash down,” and the preview for The Flash #39 shows this battle getting underway in the Arrow-Cave. Wally’s inner monologue reveals that he’s having to keep his guard up with Jon Kent (who hasn’t yet become Tomorrow Man in this appearance), Wonder Woman, Martian Manhunter, and Red Tornado in particular, with Aquaman also in the mix alongside Green Arrow.

In a recent development, in addition to Jon, Diana, and J’onn having their own levels of super speed, these three also have additional abilities that worry Wally. Jon has heat vision, freeze breath, and shoots lightning from his hands; Diana is a “divine Amazon” armed with the Lasso of Truth and her trademark projectile tiara, and J’onn is gifted with super strength, shape-shifting, intangibility, and telepathy. As for Red Tornado, although he’s still a hologram, his android brain can calculate almost all of Wally’s moves and order his teammates where and how they should attack next.

Industry observers note that though Wally manages to take Red Tornado out of the picture by tossing his hologram projector away, this is still a tough fight for him. If his concentration breaks for even a second, then Jon, Wonder Woman, and Martian Manhunter will have an opening to neutralize Flash. Plus, although they don’t have super speed, there’s still the possibility that Green Arrow and/or Aquaman might find a way to strike him.

It has been revealed that still, it’s reasonable for these Justice Leaguer members to be troubled about Wally. Along with the ethical implications of his precognition, Red Tornado revealed that The Flash’s 24/7 use of the Speed Force is unintentionally creating wormholes within his pain receptors. Wally was close to acquiescing and giving up using his precognitive abilities, but when Green Arrow kept talking trash and pulled out an arrow meant to remove Flash’s powers, he did a 180, hence why the battle began.

According to recent reports, the good news is that Wally will lose his precognition by the end of The Flash #39. The bad news is that, per the solicitation for The Flash #40, he’ll lose all his other powers, too. It looks like Green Arrow’s speed-sapping arrow will indeed be used, but unfortunately, but this comes right as Wally is certain that his prophetic visions foreshadow something that will “threaten the survival of civilization itself.” Without his powers, he’ll have to convince his wife and superpowered kids to help him “fix everything.”.

The Flash #39 will be released Wednesday, November 25 by DC Comics.

Sources indicate that amazon's early Black Friday 2026 sale is already bringing some substantial discounts on smart home devices, with savings ranging from $23 to $700 across security cameras, video doorbells, smart locks, home security systems, thermostats, and robot vacuums. Several products are more than 50% off, including indoor security cameras from Blink, Ring, and Arlo, while higher-end devices from Eufy and Roborock are seeing price cuts of hundreds of dollars.

In a recent development, you can also check out our other Black Friday coverage for more tech deals as the sale continues. For now, here are some of the best early Black Friday 2026 smart home deals worth checking out.

Named the best security camera of 2024 by PCMag, TP-Link’s Tapo MagCam C425 is now down to $54.99 from $89.99, making it an affordable option for keeping an eye on your driveway, backyard, or front entrance without having to run power cables. It records in 2K resolution and runs on a rechargeable battery, while support for microSD storage lets you save footage locally without paying for a cloud subscription.

Industry observers note that reolink’s 4K Solar Security Camera is down to $144.99 from $229.99, saving you $85. It connects over 4G LTE, so it can keep watch over a barn, vacation home, construction sites, or other areas where a regular wifi security camera won't work because there’s no home network to join. Its microSD support lets you save footage locally without a cloud subscription—you will, however, need an active cellular data plan to get the camera online.

Eufy’s SoloCam S340 is $119.99, down from $219.99, and it pairs a 3K wide-angle lens with a 2K telephoto lens, giving you a view of the whole yard and a closer look at faces or packages at the same time. The camera pans a full 360 degrees and tilts to follow people as they move, and the included solar panel keeps it charged in a sunny spot. Footage is stored on 8GB of built-in storage with no monthly fee—one of the reasons why the S340 earned an Editors’ Choice award in PCMag’s review.

Sources indicate that eufy’s Video Doorbell E340 is $99.99, down from $169.99, and it uses two cameras to cover your front door, with one recording visitors in 2K and the other pointing down at the doorstep to keep an eye on deliveries. It also has color night vision, a removable rechargeable battery, and 8GB of built-in storage for recording footage without a cloud subscription. You can read more about its performance in PCMag's review.

Industry observers note that at $28, down from $79.99, the second-generation Arlo Wireless Video Doorbell 2K is one of the more affordable ways to keep an eye on your front door. Its 2K camera provides a detailed view of visitors, while the wide field of view helps capture packages left near your doorstep—making it easy to see why PCMag named it the best video doorbell of 2024.

Recent findings suggest that the Blink Battery Doorbell 2K+ is down to $34.99 from $79.99. It records in 2K resolution and offers a head-to-toe view, so you can see who's at the door as well as any packages left on your doorstep. And since it runs on batteries, installation is relatively simple, especially for renters or anyone who doesn't want to deal with doorbell wiring. For more on it, check out PCMag’s review.

Recent findings suggest that the Eufy Security FamiLock E34 is down to $179.99 from $279.99, saving you $100 on a smart lock that uses palm vein recognition to unlock your door, which Eufy states takes just 0.6 seconds. It can store palm data for up to 50 people locally, making it convenient for households with multiple people, while PIN codes and app-based controls give you other ways to get inside. You also get built-in wifi and compatibility with Apple Home, Alexa, Google Home, and Matter.

In a recent development, the Ultraloq Bolt Fingerprint smart lock is $139.99, down from $199.99, and it replaces your deadbolt with a lock you can open using a fingerprint, a keypad code, or the U Home app over built-in wifi. It can also unlock automatically as you walk up to the door, using your phone’s location. PCMag named it the best smart lock of 2024.

Recent findings suggest that simpliSafe’s DIY 8-piece Wireless Home Security System is down to $119.99 from $209.99, making it a relatively affordable starting point for securing multiple entry points around your home. The kit includes a base station, keypad, entry sensors, a motion sensor, and a panic button, so you can monitor doors, windows, and movement inside the house. For more details, check out PCMag’s in-depth review.

The Arlo Home Security System is $142.49, down from $199.99, and this starter kit pairs a Keypad Sensor Hub with two All-in-One Sensors, each of which can be set to detect motion, open doors and windows, water leaks, and other events across eight functions. It runs in the same Arlo Secure app as Arlo’s cameras and doorbells, which makes it a natural addition for homes that already use them. For more on its features and performance, check out PCMag’s review.

In a recent development, at just $15.99, down from $39.99, the Blink Mini 2K+ is one of the cheapest ways to add indoor monitoring to your smart home. This compact plug-in camera records in 2K resolution, and also supports motion alerts, two-way audio, and Alexa integration. PCMag has a review of the Blink Mini 2K+.

The Ring Indoor Cam 2K is seeing a substantial discount, dropping from $59.99 to $24.99. It records in 2K resolution, giving you a clear view of rooms and hallways, while two-way audio lets you speak to family members or pets through the Ring app. There's also a built-in privacy cover that blocks the camera when you don't want it recording, along with support for other Ring and Alexa devices. You can read more about its features and performance in PCMag's review.

According to recent reports, arlo’s Essential Pan Tilt Indoor Cam 2K is $18.99, down from $49.99, and it’s part of the lineup Arlo released in 2025, with a motorized head that rotates a full 360 degrees and tilts 180 degrees so one camera can cover an entire room. This PCMag review goes into more detail on how it performs.

It has been revealed that the Sensi Smart Thermostat ST55 is at the moment $79, down from $129.99, and is a good option for anyone looking to control their home's heating and cooling from a phone—it lets you create schedules, adjust temperatures remotely, and use geofencing to make changes based on whether you're home or away. It also works with several popular smart home platforms, including Alexa, Google Assistant, and Samsung SmartThings, plus Apple HomeKit when a C-wire is connected, notes this PCMag review.

According to recent reports, the Amazon Smart Thermostat is a more affordable alternative at $56.99, down from $79.99. It works with Alexa to let you adjust temperatures through voice commands or the Alexa app, where you can also set schedules and automate temperature changes based on your routines. For more on its setup and features, check out PCMag's review.

According to recent reports, ecovacs’ Deebot X8 Pro Omni is down to $699.99 from $1,099.99, saving you $400 on a robot vacuum that takes care of both vacuuming and mopping. It uses a roller mop that continuously rinses itself with clean water as it works and extends outward to clean along walls and furniture. You also get 18,000Pa of suction and a self-maintaining dock that empties the dustbin, washes the mop with hot water, and dries it afterward. For more on its cleaning performance, check out PCMag’s review.

Recent findings suggest that the Roborock Qrevo CurvX has dropped to $799.99 from $1,499.99, saving you $700. It’s a 2025 revision to the Qrevo Curv that raises suction from 18,500Pa to 22,000Pa and slims the robot to 3.14 inches tall so it fits under more couches and beds, while keeping the AdaptiLift chassis for climbing thresholds and a dock that washes the mop pads with hot water. This PCMag review covers the original Qrevo Curv, which should be a useful reference for the design and dock the two models share.

According to recent reports, nowadays, both large retailers and small businesses compete for Black Friday shoppers, so you can expect practically every store to run sales through Monday, Nov. 30, 2026. The “best” sales depend on your needs, but in general, the biggest discounts tend to come from larger retailers who can afford lower prices: think places like Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy, and Home Depot. You can find all the best sales from major retailers on our Black Friday coverage.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The world has changed quite a lot over the last six years, with ups and downs in every facet of human existence, but during all that time, there’s been one thing we can all agree has been as great as ever: the movies. Sure, there have been plenty of terrible movies made in the 2020s, but there have also been some truly amazing works of art — films that transcend their time, place, and medium to deliver powerful messages that become an indelible part of our shared culture.

They may not all have made a great mark at the box office, but each of these masterpieces has pushed the boundaries of cinema, challenging preconceptions and transforming the way we see the world. Award-winners and hidden gems alike, these films may be relatively recent, but they’re classics-to-be that are sure to be remembered with warmth and adoration by future generations of audiences and filmmakers. Without further ado, here’s our ranked selection of the eight most perfect movies of the last six years.

A sci-fi comedy drama written, directed, and co-produced by Wes Anderson, Asteroid City follows a group of students and their parents who have gathered at the titular desert town for the Annual Junior Stargazer Convention in 1955. When certain unforeseen circumstances develop, leading to a military quarantine, it affects the lives of all the people attending the convention. The film’s ensemble cast includes Scarlett Johansson, Jason Schwartzman, Bryan Cranston, Jeffrey Wright, Tom Hanks, Tilda Swinton, Margot Robbie, Edward Norton, Adrien Brody, and Tony Revolori in major roles.

Through his hallmark visual and narrative styles, Anderson brings his unique cinematic voice to the UFO sighting myths of the post-war American Southwest. Presented through an electric blend of comedy, romance, drama, and a bit of sci-fi, Asteroid City works like a vibrant vignette about art, grief, and human connection, framed by an inventive meta-narrative. Headlining the summer of 2022, Asteroid City earned critical acclaim with its poignant themes, artistic storytelling, and quirky characters, and it’s widely considered to be Wes Anderson’s best film since The Grand Budapest Hotel.

In a recent development, written and directed by Damien Chazelle, Babylon is an epic period black comedy drama that chronicles the rise and fall of several characters in the Golden Age of Hollywood as the industry prepares itself for the transition from silent films to talkies. Centering on Nellie LaRoy, a brash and ambitious starlet, and Manny, a resourceful Mexican immigrant dreaming of making it in Hollywood, the film explores the era of unbridled decadence and depravity that marked a turning point in the industry’s history. The movie boasts a star-studded ensemble cast, with Brad Pitt, Margot Robbie, Diego Calva, Jean Smart, Jovan Adepo, and Li Jun Li in major roles.

Sources indicate that capturing a watershed moment in the history of cinema through a wild tale of decadence, depravity, and outrageousness, Damien Chazelle pays his most heartfelt and emotional tribute to cinema while simultaneously critiquing its excesses and flaws. The film examines the destructive, rapidly changing, and often brutal nature of showbiz while simultaneously highlighting its magical, lasting power. Even though it met with divisive reviews and reactions on its release, Babylon has been widely praised for the music composition by Justin Hurwitz and is now considered to be a cult film of the decade.

Sources indicate that written and directed by Robert Eggers, Nosferatu is a Gothic horror reimagination of 1922’s Nosferatu: A Symphony of Horror, which in turn is an unofficial adaptation of Bram Stoker’s Dracula. In the film, Ellen, a young woman, accidentally connects with the spirit of a terrifying vampire who becomes obsessed with her, terrorizing everyone in his way as he comes to claim her. Lily-Rose Depp stars as Ellen with Bill Skarsgård as the titular monster. The movie also features Nicholas Hoult, Aaron Taylor-Johnson, Emma Corrin, and Willem Dafoe in other lead roles.

It has been revealed that gorgeously shot in black-and-white, Nosferatu is a cinematic treat that draws elements and inspiration from German Expressionism, silent cinema, and 1960s/'70s horror. Unlike the classic adaptations of Dracula, Nosferatu is more intricate in its storytelling, diving deeper into the concept, characters, and horror. A remarkable combination of psychological horror and supernatural gore, the movie is Eggers’ highest-grossing and most critically acclaimed film so far, and was widely hailed as one of the best films of 2024.

Four worlds and four completely different ideas of what a good life looks like. This is where you belong, what it would ask of you, and what you would get back in return.

You belong somewhere old enough that the mountains have names and somebody can still tell you who gave them. Middle-earth is for people who think the right thing is worth doing even when it will not be finished in their lifetime.

You want the sea, a crew, and absolutely nobody telling you where you are allowed to go. The Grand Line is the world for people whose main ambition in life is finding out what is over there.

Sources indicate that you would rather be feared and useful than liked and useless. The Continent is a world where the monsters are the straightforward part of the job and the people are where it all gets complicated.

You want the myths to be real and loose in the actual world, and you want to find out at about thirteen that you were never anywhere near as ordinary as everybody kept telling you.

In a recent development, directed by Yorgos Lanthimos, Poor Things is a reimagining of Alasdair Gray’s novel, in turn a reinterpretation of Mary Shelley’s Frankenstein. An epic black comedy fantasy, the film follows the journey of self-discovery of Bella Baxter, a woman who is brought to life by an eccentric scientist. Beginning with her life as an infant inside an adult body, the movie follows Bella as she grows into her own person, seeking knowledge, adventure, love, and sexual awakening on a wild globe-trotting romp with a degenerate lawyer. Emma Stone stars as Bella, with Willem Dafoe, Mark Ruffalo, Ramy Youssef, Christopher Abbott, and Suzy Bemba in significant roles.

Sources indicate that fierce and feminine, Poor Things is a delightfully weird take on the Frankenstein story, translated through a woman’s discovery of her freedom and finding her place in a chaotic world. Lanthimos’s unconventional storytelling takes shape through its surreal style, whimsical artistry, and dark, biting humor, not to mention the beautiful cinematography that leaves the audience in awe with every frame. Elevated by Emma Stone’s mystifying and brazen performance that earned her an Academy Award, Poor Things is easily one of the finest films of the 2020s so far.

Sources indicate that an absurdist sci-fi action comedy directed by Daniel Kwan and Daniel Scheinert, Everything Everywhere All at Once follows the fantastic multiversal experiences of Evelyn Wang, a Chinese-American woman struggling with her business, stale marriage, and complicated family dynamics. During a tax audit, Evelyn suddenly finds herself caught up in a crisis involving alternative universes and is called on to stop an evil entity from destroying everything that exists. Michelle Yeoh stars as Evelyn, with Stephanie Hsu, Ke Huy Quan, Jamie Lee Curtis, and James Hong in supporting roles.

In a recent development, A wild sci-fi adventure, Everything Everywhere All at Once fantastically incorporates motifs and elements of everything and everyone that inspired it, from Wong Kar-wai and Mary-Jane Rubenstein to the video game Everything and the children’s book Sylvester and the Magic Pebble. Using strong elements of surrealism, absurdism, and existentialism in its narrative, the film presents a heartfelt story of a woman’s journey of reconnecting with herself. Through this, the film explores broader themes of Asian American identity. Acclaimed for its conceptual and visual magnitude, Everything Everywhere All at Once ranks among the top sci-fi films of the last decade, and it broke several records and earned numerous accolades.

Written, directed, and produced by Paul Thomas Anderson, One Battle After Another is a black comedy action thriller that reimagines Thomas Pynchon’s 1990 novel Vineland. The film follows Bob Ferguson, a has-been revolutionary who lives off the grid with his young daughter, Willa. When he is unexpectedly separated from her, Bob is forced to return to his roots and embark on a paranoia-fueled search for his child while dodging a ruthless military officer. Leonardo DiCaprio and Chase Infiniti star as the father-daughter duo, with Teyana Taylor, Sean Penn, Benicio del Toro, Regina Hall, and more starring in key roles.

One of the most celebrated films of 2025, One Battle After Another balances a high-energy narrative and screwball humor with the intimate parent-child relationship at its heart. Fun and exciting, with strong performances and well-choreographed action pieces, it is arguably one of the most entertaining films of the 2020s so far, and unarguably one of the most acclaimed films of Anderson’s career. One Battle After Another is noted for the phenomenal reception and acclaim it received, earning 458 nominations and 227 wins, including six Academy Awards.

Recent findings suggest that the first Oscar-winning Latvian film, Flow is an animated dystopian adventure film directed and co-written by Gints Zilbalodis in his feature film debut. The independent animated movie follows the story of a solitary, anonymous cat whose home gets destroyed by a massive flood, forcing it to seek refuge on a boat. Surrounded by creatures of various species on the boat, the lonely feline is forced to adapt to its new environment and cohabitants. The film is noted for featuring no dialogue, and the movie takes inspiration from Zilbalodis’s previous work, Aqua, as well as the work of French filmmaker/mime artist Jacques Tati and the anime series Future Boy Conan.

A tender, melancholic film with a post-apocalyptic theme, Flow brings nostalgia and hope to the narrative while treating the audience with spectacular, dreamy visuals. Told through the perspective of a solitary cat, the narrative successfully expresses the core sentiments without needing the help of sentimentality or words, speaking volumes in its silence. Flow made history as the most-viewed film ever in Latvian theaters and became the first Latvian film to be nominated at the Academy Awards, where it won the award for Best Animated Feature. It also received the Golden Globe Award in the same category.

A period horror film written, directed, and produced by Ryan Coogler, Sinners follows the story of twin brothers, Elijah "Smoke" and Elias "Stack" Moore, who return to their home in 1932 Mississippi after seven years in Chicago working for the mob. As the brothers set out to make a upcoming life with new dreams, an evil supernatural entity starts terrorizing the town, threatening their lives. Michael B. Jordan plays the dual roles of Smoke and Stack, alongside Hailee Steinfeld, Jack O'Connell, Wunmi Mosaku, Jayme Lawson, Omar Benson Miller, Delroy Lindo, and Miles Caton in his film debut.

According to recent reports, sinners was an instant commercial and critical hit when it premiered, earning universal acclaim for its masterful and artistic storytelling, acting, cinematography, and music composition. Not only is Michael B. Jordan’s gripping performance in the movie one of his career bests, but the film has also earned recognition as Coogler’s most acclaimed film so far, winning several accolades, including a record 16 Academy Award nominations, of which it won four. Sinners also made history with cinematographer Autumn Durald Arkapaw becoming the first woman of color in Academy history to be nominated, and the first woman ever to win an Academy Award for Best Cinematography.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, even though critics appeared to agree that one specific trope had no place in the horror genre during the 2000s and 2010s, Netflix has since proven that this maxim was unfairly dismissive of the classic convention. When MTV’s Scream: The Series debuted in 2015, fans of the movie franchise took to the Internet to share their collective dismay about one major change the show made to the original Scream formula.

According to recent reports, unlike the protagonists of the first four Scream movies, the heroes of Scream: The Series didn’t make self-aware comments that acknowledged the existence of horror movies in-universe. While the main characters of Netflix’s zombie horror All of Us Are Dead frequently compared their plight to a classic zombie movie like Train to Busan, Scream: The Series played its teen mystery more straight. As a result, critics complained, the show was little more than Pretty Little Liars with added jump scares.

This critique might not have been entirely unfair, since the self-referential humor of the Scream movies was a big part of what made them so popular in the first place. However, the sly dig at so-called “jump scares” is a telling one that reveals a lot about the attitudes of reviewers, and a great many horror fans, during the 2010s and 2000s. Throughout these decades, jump scares were often used as shorthand to refer to cheap, tacky horror, until Netflix hits like The Haunting of Hill House, Marianne, and Something Very Bad Is Going to Happen redeemed their reputation.

It has been revealed that in the early 2000s, the chaotic, fast-cut editing style of action horror movies like Thirteen Ghosts, Ghosts of Mars, 2005’s Doom and Alone in the Dark, and the original Resident Evil led to widespread disdain for what were termed “jump scares.” Jump scares had, of course, been commonplace since as early as 1960’s Psycho, 1974’s The Texas Chain Saw Massacre, and 1978’s Halloween. However, quick cutting and computer assisted imagery allowed for fast flashes of gory horror that were viewed as uniquely cheap “cheats” by many critics.

Industry observers note that this style hit its nadir with the deluge of 2000s horror remakes. 2003’s The Texas Chainsaw Massacre, 2005’s The Amityville Horror, 2005’s House of Wax, and 2006’s The Hills Have Eyes and When A Stranger Calls all relied heavily on this hyperactive editing style. Where later re-imaginings like Prime Video’s Carrie were praised for rewriting their source material, these redoes were often accused of taking existing stories and simply adding a slew of cheap shocks to reinvigorate franchise's brand.

According to recent reports, while there might have been some validity to complaints about the lack of originality in the 2000s remake era, jump scares themselves were typically uncritically viewed as an indicator of the genre’s devolution into artless shock value. However, throughout the late 2010s and early 2020s, Netflix’s best horror reveals did a lot to reverse this view, proving that jump scares could be an ingredient in horror stories that were not just worthwhile, but truly great.

Recent findings suggest that the Haunting of Hill House, 2019’s critically acclaimed horror Marianne, 2023’s Fall of the House of Usher, 2026’s Something Very Bad Is Going to Happen, and even All of Us Are Dead all feature jump scares that advance their stories while also scaring viewers senseless. Some of the most infamously terrifying moments in The Haunting of Hill House are also pivotal moments in the character arcs of the show’s protagonists, meaning writer/director Mike Flanagan’s tragic family saga wouldn’t make sense without these jarring shocks.

With this string of well-deserved critical hits, the streaming service proved beyond a shadow of a doubt that an acclaimed horror show could absolutely rely on jump scares without sacrificing depth and complexity. Throughout the 2000s and 2010s, the unspoken implication that was carried by the term “jump scare” was that the momentary shock was inherently shallow, devoid of narrative and thematic value.

Sources indicate that however, Netflix thoroughly debunked this claim. In particular, The Haunting of Hill House and Marianne use jump scares judiciously in stories that are still character-driven and intelligent, disproving the classic adage that a horror movie or TV show is either atmospheric and thoughtful, or reliant only on silly, superficial jump scares. One example from The Haunting of Hill House illustrates this particularly well.

In episode 8 of frequent Stephen King collaborator Flanagan’s miniseries, Shirley and Theo’s drive to Hill House devolves into a screaming match about infidelity, buried family secrets, and intergenerational wounds. The pair are deeply immersed in a furious fight when the grey-faced, empty-eyed ghost of their late sister Nell bursts out from the space between their seats and screams, terrifying the audience and the sisters in equal measure.

While a lazy analysis would term this moment a jump scare and move on, the scene has a thematic and narrative value that proves it is perfectly placed in Flanagan’s story. In thematic terms, Nell is quite literally only able to access her voice and make herself heard over her louder, more confident older sisters after her death. In narrative terms, the shock jolts Shirley and Theo out of their interpersonal conflict and reminds them why they are returning to the eponymous cursed home in the first place.

Industry observers note that while it would be a while before HBO Max’s It spinoff Welcome to Derry arrived on the streaming service in 2025, The Haunting of Hill House’s ingenious jump scare still laid the groundwork for the prequel’s judicious use of this technique despite its ignominious reputation. In 2022, Flanagan intentionally set a record for the most jump scares in one episode of TV, as a self-aware joke, in The Midnight Club’s pilot episode.

Years later, other major critical hits from other streaming services, like Welcome to Derry and Peacock’s Friday the 13th prequel Crystal Lake, followed suit. Both Welcome to Derry and Crystal Lake were starry, expensive productions with impressive casts and aspirations to ground their respective franchises in believable character drama as well as gruesome horror.

According to recent reports, thus, these were the exact sort of demonstrates that would typically be discouraged from including jump scares, lest they be written off as cheap, trashy horror. Fortunately, thanks to Netflix hits like The Haunting of Hill House and Marianne, horror TV creators now know there has never been anything wrong with giving viewers a good jolt.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You’re almost ready for Grand Theft Auto VI. You’ve preloaded the game on your console, you’ve taken the next month off work, and you’ve locked your phone in a Faraday cage and set it adrift at sea. You’re prepared to lock in, and you haven’t forgotten a thing…right? Well, just to make sure, here are the most notable tips to optimize your setup before you fire up the most anticipated game of the decade.

In a recent development, GTA 6 is absurdly large. According to Rockstar, you’ll need up to 212GB of storage space. For high-end consoles like the PS5 Pro, that’s more than 10% of the available storage space, and close to half the space on the more budget-conscious Xbox Series S. There’s a good chance you’ll have to delete something to make room.

Alternatively, it’s pretty easy to add more storage (if you can afford it). External SSDs are probably the cheapest route, though you’ll want to make sure to use a high-speed USB cable to connect it. It’s even worth shopping around for alternate models of SSD. For example, at the time of writing, the popular 2TB WD_BLACK external drive was close to $200, but the exact same drive in pink was $132.

You can also directly upgrade the storage of your console with expansion drives. The Xbox Series X|S supports proprietary expansion cards, while the PS5 and PS5 Pro can accept most M.2 internal SSDs. These will generally be faster, since they plug directly into the console via higher-speed connections than a drive hooked up via USB.

Let’s face it: Half the fun of any sandbox game is the weird, unique stuff that happens to only you. So you’re probably going to be hitting that “record recent gameplay” button more often than usual. While you’re cleaning up your storage space (or adding more), make sure to account for all the video clips you might want to save.

Industry observers note that file size of video clips depends on a lot of factors, but 4K recordings can generally take up to 0.5GB per minute of footage. You can cut that down by saving footage in 1080p instead, but either way you’ll want to leave a little extra space.

It has been revealed that game footage is also a pretty good place to look if you need to make room on your console and don’t want to delete any games. Be honest with yourself: You don’t need all those clips from Horizon Forbidden West you saved four years ago. Dive into the settings on your console and find the biggest media files you forgot you even had on there.

Industry observers note that according to Rockstar, GTA 6 will be targeting 30fps across consoles at launch, which is pretty low as modern AAA games go. Part of the reason for that is all the processing power going to rendering a complex environment, but it also means you won’t need a fancy high frame rate TV or monitor any time soon to get the most out of it. Still, it couldn’t hurt to check a few settings on your display.

First, make sure you’re using a higher refresh rate than 30Hz. While the game is targeting 30fps, it is technically capable of more, so if your console can keep up, you don’t want to accidentally bottleneck your frames. This setting will vary by device, so check the manual that came with your screen.

Recent findings suggest that also, make sure you have HDR enabled on your hardware. There’s a good chance this is already turned on for your TV, but sometimes other devices can switch display modes if they only support SDR. The game will help you calibrate your HDR settings for GTA 6 specifically when you launch it, but only if it detects HDR compatibility in the first place.

It has been revealed that if you’re planning to buy a console specifically for GTA 6, this might be one of those rare instances where a PS5 Pro really is worth the upgrade. According to Rockstar, certain features like ray-traced shadows will only be available on the Pro version of Sony’s console.

More importantly, the PS5 Pro version supports PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (or PSSR), which upscales lower-resolution images to get better detail and higher frame rates out of the same hardware. Given that GTA 6 is already starting at a meager target of 30fps on most consoles, anything that can give your frame rate a boost is probably going to feel like a welcome improvement over the baseline.

Recent findings suggest that I’ll tell you a secret as someone who’s spent a lot of time testing different game controllers: Most of the time, you really don’t need an expensive “elite” controller. Most of the time. I don’t buy into the idea that a taller control stick is going to make you an esports athlete. It can be nice to have, but it’s not a game changer. What does matter is customizing your controls, especially for long gaming sessions.

It has been revealed that the DualSense Edge wireless controller is a favorite of mine, mainly because of the rear paddles and adjustable triggers. The former lets you map any button to a rear lever that you can access with your fingers underneath the controller, which can often ease some of the wrist strain of awkward button combos. And the adjustable triggers let you activate the buttons with less motion, again reducing repetitive stress.

The Xbox Elite Series 2 controller has similar features for the Xbox, as well as custom caps for the D-pad. Both consoles’ versions of pro controllers are more expensive than the standard ones, but if you’re planning to game for many hours, it can be worth it to get a controller that’s more comfortable for you.

According to recent reports, if you have an Xbox One, you don’t necessarily have to upgrade your console to play GTA 6, but you might want to take a look at your network. GTA 6 will be available on Xbox Cloud Gaming on day one, and you’ll be able to stream the game to an Xbox One console (as long as you purchase Cloud playtime as well or get some with your Game Pass subscription). This is the only way to play on a console older than the current generation, so if you don’t want to shell out for newly introduced hardware, this might be your best bet.

Xbox recommends a minimum of a 20Mbps connection to run cloud gaming, but more is obviously better. If you can connect your console to a wired Ethernet connection, that would be better and provide more stability. If you can’t connect a cable, then at least make sure you’re well within range of your wifi router, and try to limit any other bandwidth-hogging applications on the network while you’re playing.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Last month Apple announced big updates coming to Apple Creator Studio in November, and those updates have just arrived, headlined by the addition of MotionVFX in Final Cut Pro and a lot more.

When Apple unveiled its new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR last month, it highlighted several big updates coming to Apple Creator Studio’s app suite.

Logic Pro got its update earlier in November, which introduced new AI features and also the first example of Apple charging for increased AI access via ‘intelligence usage packs.’.

Now today after about a two-week gap, the rest of the Apple Creator Studio updates are rolling out on the App Store.

Pixelmator Pro has added a upcoming Generate Fill feature, which “lets creators transform selected areas of an image using natural language.” And you can edit images from a Final Cut Pro project using Pixelmator’s tools.

Updates for Pages, Keynote, and Numbers are rolling out too with an Intelligent Assistant feature, as well as smaller releases for Apple’s other pro utilities.

To read more on the new updates, see our previous coverage here.
